title.zh: 卷67 列傳第32 虞世基 裴蘊 裴矩
title.en: Volume 67 Biographies 32: Yun Shiji, Pei Yun, Pei Ju
title.raw: 卷67 列傳第32 虞世基 裴蘊 裴矩 Volume 67 Biographies 32: Yun Shiji, Pei Yun, Pei Ju

sentences.zh: 隋書卷六十七列傳第三十二

translations.literal: Book of Sui, Volume 67, Biographies 32
translations.idiomatic: Book of Sui, Volume 67, Biographies 32

sentences.zh: 虞世基

translations.literal: Yu Shiji
translations.idiomatic: Yu Shiji

sentences.zh: 虞世基，字茂世，會稽余姚人也。

translations.literal: Yu Shiji, style name Maoshi, was a native of Yuyao in Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Shiji, whose style name was Maoshi, came from Yuyao in Kuaiji prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父荔，陳太子中庶子。

translations.literal: His father Li was Junior Mentor to the Chen crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: His father Li had served as Junior Mentor to the crown prince of Chen.

sentences.zh: 世基幼沉靜，喜慍不形于色，博學有高才，兼善草隸。

translations.literal: Shiji from youth was deep and calm; joy and anger did not show on his face. He was broadly learned with lofty talent, and was also skilled in cursive and clerical script.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood Shiji was reserved and even-tempered; neither pleasure nor anger showed on his face. He was widely read and exceptionally gifted, and excelled at both cursive and clerical calligraphy.

sentences.zh: 陳中書令孔奐見而曰：「南金之貴，屬在斯人。

translations.literal: Kong Huan, Director of the Secretariat in Chen, saw him and said: "The preciousness of southern gold rests in this man.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Huan, Director of the Secretariat under Chen, met him and remarked, "The finest gold of the south belongs to this man alone.

sentences.zh: 」少傅徐陵聞其名，召之，世基不往。

translations.literal: " The Junior Tutor Xu Ling heard his name and summoned him; Shiji did not go.
translations.idiomatic: " When Junior Tutor Xu Ling heard of his reputation he sent for him, but Shiji declined to come.

sentences.zh: 後因公會，陵一見而奇之，顧謂朝士曰：「當今潘、陸也。

translations.literal: Later, at a public gathering, Ling saw him once and marveled at him, turning to the court gentlemen and saying: "The Pan and Lu of our day.
translations.idiomatic: Later, at an official assembly, Xu Ling took one look at him and was astonished; turning to the court officials he said, "Here are our own Pan Yue and Lu Ji.

sentences.zh: 」因以弟女妻焉。

translations.literal: " Therefore he gave him his younger brother's daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: " He accordingly gave him his younger brother's daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 仕陳，釋褐建安王法曹參軍事，曆祠部殿中二曹郎、太子中舍人。

translations.literal: He entered service in Chen, first taking office as Legal Bureau Attendant for the Prince of Jian'an, and passed through the two bureau posts of Sacrifices Officer and Palace Attendant and Crown Prince Household Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Under Chen he began his career as legal aide to the Prince of Jian'an, then served successively in the Sacrifices and Palace bureaus and as attendant in the crown prince's household.

sentences.zh: 遷中庶子、散騎常侍、尚書左丞。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Junior Mentor, Regular Attendant of Cavalry, and Left Assistant Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Junior Mentor, Regular Attendant of Cavalry, and Left Assistant Director in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 陳主嘗于莫府山校獵，令世基作《講武賦》，於坐奏之曰：

translations.literal: The Chen ruler once conducted a military hunt at Mofu Mountain and ordered Shiji to compose "Rhapsody on Military Exercises"; he presented it at the gathering, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Once when the Chen emperor held a martial hunt on Mount Mofu, he had Shiji compose a "Rhapsody on Military Exercises" and recite it before the assembled company:

sentences.zh: 夫玩居常者，未可論匡濟之功；

translations.literal: Those who merely enjoy ordinary living cannot be judged for the merit of aiding the realm;
translations.idiomatic: Those content with ordinary ease cannot be judged for the merit of saving the realm;

sentences.zh: 應變通者，然後見帝王之略。

translations.literal: only those who respond to change and adapt reveal the strategy of an emperor.
translations.idiomatic: only those who meet change with resourcefulness reveal a true emperor's strategy.

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why is this so?

sentences.zh: 化有文質，進讓殊風，世或澆淳，解張累務。

translations.literal: Transformation has civil and martial aspects; advance and yielding have different styles; ages may be thin or pure, loosening or tightening successive tasks.
translations.idiomatic: Civilization has its cultured and martial sides; advance and restraint follow different customs; ages may run thin or deep, and policy must loosen or tighten accordingly.

sentences.zh: 雖複順紀合符之後，望雲就日之君，且修戰於版泉，亦治兵於丹浦。

translations.literal: Even after the age when the calendar accorded and omens matched, and even for rulers whom the people looked to as clouds to the sun, one still drilled troops at Banquan and also trained armies at Danpu.
translations.idiomatic: Even after the age when heaven's signs aligned, and even for rulers whom the people revered as they do the sun, the Yellow Emperor still drilled troops at Banquan and King Wu still marshaled armies at Danpu.

sentences.zh: 是知文德武功，蓋因時而並用，經邦創制，固與俗而推移。

translations.literal: Thus one knows that civil virtue and martial achievement are employed together according to the times, and that governing the state and establishing institutions surely shift with custom.
translations.idiomatic: From this we know that civil virtue and martial achievement are deployed together as the times require, and that governing the state and founding institutions must move with the customs of the age.

sentences.zh: 所以樹鴻名，垂大訓，拱揖百靈，包舉六合，其唯聖人乎！

translations.literal: Therefore to raise a great name, hand down great instruction, bow to the hundred spirits, and embrace the six directions—this is none but the sage!
translations.idiomatic: To raise a great name, hand down enduring instruction, bow before the hundred spirits, and embrace all within the six directions—only the sage can do this!

sentences.zh: 鶉火之歲，皇上禦宇之四年也。

translations.literal: In the year of the Quail Fire asterism, it was the fourth year of His Majesty's rule over the realm.
translations.idiomatic: In the year marked by the Quail Fire asterism, it was the fourth year of His Majesty's reign.

sentences.zh: 萬物交泰，九有乂安，俗躋仁壽，民資日用。

translations.literal: The ten thousand things reached great harmony; the nine regions were well governed; custom rose to benevolence and longevity; the people drew on daily abundance.
translations.idiomatic: The ten thousand things flourished in harmony; the nine regions were at peace; customs approached benevolence and longevity; the people enjoyed their daily needs.

sentences.zh: 然而足食足兵，猶載懷于履薄；

translations.literal: Yet though food and arms were sufficient, he still bore in mind walking on thin ice;
translations.idiomatic: Yet though food and arms were ample, he still bore in mind the peril of walking on thin ice;

sentences.zh: 可久可大，尚懍乎於禦朽。

translations.literal: what could long endure and grow great, he still feared as one who repairs rotten timbers.
translations.idiomatic: what might long endure and grow great, he still guarded with the caution of one repairing rotten timbers.

sentences.zh: 至如昆吾遠贐，肅慎奇賝，史不絕書，府無虛月。

translations.literal: As for Kunwu's distant tribute and Sushen's rare gifts, the histories never ceased recording them, and the storehouses knew no empty month.
translations.idiomatic: Tribute arrived from distant Kunwu and rare gifts from Sushen; the histories record them without cease, and the treasuries knew no idle month.

sentences.zh: 貝胄雍弧之用，犀渠闕鞏之殷，鑄名劍于尚方，積雕戈於武庫。

translations.literal: Shell helmets and ceremonial bows were in use; rhinoceros-hide shields and tower shields were abundant; famous swords were cast at the Imperial Workshop, and carved halberds piled in the armory.
translations.idiomatic: Shell helmets and ceremonial bows stood ready; rhinoceros-hide shields and tower shields filled the arsenals; famous swords were cast at the Imperial Workshop, and carved halberds stocked the armory.

sentences.zh: 熊羆百萬，貔豹千群，利盡五材，威加四海。

translations.literal: Bear and brown bear troops numbered in the millions, leopard and panther hosts in the thousands; the sharpness of the five materials was fully deployed, and might extended over the four seas.
translations.idiomatic: Armies bold as bears and brown bears numbered in the millions, hosts fierce as leopards and panthers in the thousands; every weapon's edge was honed, and might reached across the four seas.

sentences.zh: 爰于農隙，有事春蒐，舍爵策動，觀使臣之以禮，沮勸賞罰，乃示民以知禁。

translations.literal: Then in the agricultural interval came the spring hunt: cups were set aside and merit recorded; envoys were observed for their ritual conduct; rewards and punishments were urged and restrained, thereby showing the people what was forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Then in the farming season's pause came the spring hunt: cups were set aside and merit recorded; ministers were watched for proper ritual; rewards and punishments were applied, teaching the people what the law forbade.

sentences.zh: 盛矣哉，信百王之不易，千載之一時也！

translations.literal: How magnificent! Truly an unchanging norm among the hundred kings, a moment once in a thousand years!
translations.idiomatic: How magnificent! Truly a constant among the hundred kings, a moment that comes once in a thousand years!

sentences.zh: 昔上林從幸，相如於是頌德，長楊校獵，子雲退而為賦。

translations.literal: In old times at Shanglin Park the emperor went in attendance and Xiangru thereupon praised his virtue; at Changyang the military hunt was held and Ziyun withdrew and composed a rhapsody.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago at Shanglin Park the emperor went hunting and Sima Xiangru praised his virtue; at Changyang a martial hunt was held and Yang Xiong withdrew to compose a rhapsody.

sentences.zh: 雖則體物緣情，不同年而語矣，英聲茂實，蓋可得而言焉。

translations.literal: Though in embodying things and following feeling they cannot be spoken of in the same breath, their splendid fame and abundant achievement can indeed be described.
translations.idiomatic: Though in describing things and voicing feeling they cannot quite be compared, their splendid renown and solid achievement may still be told.

sentences.zh: 其辭曰：

translations.literal: The text reads:
translations.idiomatic: The text reads:

sentences.zh: 惟則天以稽古，統資始於群分。

translations.literal: Heaven alone takes antiquity as its model and governs the beginning among the multitude of divisions.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven alone takes antiquity as its model and orders the beginning among the world's divisions.

sentences.zh: 膺錄圖而出震，樹司牧以為君。

translations.literal: He received the recorded chart and emerged in thunder, establishing overseers of the people as rulers.
translations.idiomatic: He received the celestial chart and arose in power, setting stewards of the people upon the throne.

sentences.zh: 既濟寬而濟猛，亦乃武而乃文。

translations.literal: Having crossed, he was lenient yet also stern, both martial and civil.
translations.idiomatic: Having prevailed, he was lenient yet also stern, both martial and civil in turn.

sentences.zh: 北怨勞乎殷履，南伐盛于唐勳。

translations.literal: Northern grievances were toiled over on the Yin king's footgear; southern campaigns flourished in the Tang king's merit.
translations.idiomatic: Northern foes were subdued as on King Wu of Zhou's march; southern campaigns flourished as in the achievements of King Tang.

sentences.zh: 彼周幹與夏戚，粵可得而前聞。

translations.literal: Those Zhou shields and Xia axes may be heard of from earlier ages.
translations.idiomatic: The shields of Zhou and axes of Xia may still be heard of from ages past.

sentences.zh: 我大陳之創業，乃撥亂而為武。

translations.literal: Our great Chen's founding enterprise was to quell disorder and thereby become martial.
translations.idiomatic: Our great Chen rose by quelling disorder through martial force.

sentences.zh: 戡定艱難，平壹區宇。

translations.literal: It conquered and settled hardship, and unified the realm.
translations.idiomatic: It conquered hardship and unified the realm.

sentences.zh: 從喋喋之樂推，爰蒼蒼而再補。

translations.literal: Following the music of many voices it was pushed forward; then azure Heaven mended all again.
translations.idiomatic: Following the people's acclaim it was raised up; then azure Heaven set the realm right once more.

sentences.zh: 故累仁以積德，諒重規而襲矩。

translations.literal: Therefore benevolence was piled up to accumulate virtue; surely heavy rules were inherited and repeated.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore benevolence was heaped up to accumulate virtue, and heavy precedents were inherited and followed.

sentences.zh: 惟皇帝之休烈，體徇齊之睿哲。

translations.literal: Only the emperor's glorious achievement embodies the wise sagacity of uniform fairness.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's glorious achievement embodies the wise and even-handed sagacity of a true ruler.

sentences.zh: 敷九疇而鹹敘，奄四海而有截。

translations.literal: He spread the Nine Categories and all were ordered; he covered the four seas and had a boundary.
translations.idiomatic: He spread the Nine Categories and all were set in order; he embraced the four seas and brought them to heel.

sentences.zh: 既搜揚於帝難，又文思之安安。

translations.literal: He had already sought and raised men in the emperor's difficulty, and was also cultured in thought and at peace.
translations.idiomatic: He had already sought out talent in the founding struggle, and was cultured in thought and serene in rule.

sentences.zh: 幽明請吏，俊乂在官。

translations.literal: The dark and bright realms requested officers; outstanding men held office.
translations.idiomatic: Spirits and men alike sought worthy officers; outstanding men filled the posts.

sentences.zh: 禦璿璣而七政辨，朝玉帛而萬國歡。

translations.literal: He mounted the jade armillary and the seven regulators were distinguished; the myriad states presented jade and silk and rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: He mounted the jade armillary sphere and the seven regulators were set right; the myriad states brought jade and silk and rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 昧旦丕顯，未明思治。

translations.literal: Before dawn he was greatly manifest; before light he thought of governance.
translations.idiomatic: Before dawn he was already at work; before daylight he was planning governance.

sentences.zh: 道藏往而知來，功參天而兩地。

translations.literal: The Way stored the past and knew the future; merit matched Heaven and paired with Earth.
translations.idiomatic: The Way held the past and foresaw the future; his merit matched Heaven and paired with Earth.

sentences.zh: 運聖人之上德，盡生民之能事。

translations.literal: He wielded the sage's supreme virtue and exhausted what the living people could accomplish.
translations.idiomatic: He wielded the sage's supreme virtue and brought the people's full capacity to fruition.

sentences.zh: 於是禮暢樂和，刑清政肅。

translations.literal: Thereupon ritual flowed freely and music harmonized; punishments were clear and government solemn.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon ritual flourished and music harmonized; punishments were clear and government austere.

sentences.zh: 西暨析支，東漸蟠木。

translations.literal: West to Qizhi, east reaching Panmu.
translations.idiomatic: West to Qizhi, east to Panmu—his sway reached both.

sentences.zh: 罄圖諜而效祉，漏川泉而禔福。

translations.literal: Maps and registers were exhausted in presenting blessings; rivers and springs poured forth in bestowing fortune.
translations.idiomatic: Maps and registers were filled with offerings of blessing; rivers and springs poured forth fortune.

sentences.zh: 在靈貺而必臻，亦何思而不服。

translations.literal: Where spiritual gifts were present they surely arrived; what thought would not submit?
translations.idiomatic: Where heaven's gifts were due they surely came; who could think of not submitting?

sentences.zh: 雖至治之隆平，猶戒國而強兵。

translations.literal: Though governance reached utmost peace and abundant harmony, he still warned the state and strengthened the army.
translations.idiomatic: Though rule reached utmost peace and harmony, he still guarded the state and strengthened the army.

sentences.zh: 選羽林於六郡，詔蹶張于五營。

translations.literal: He selected Forest Guards from the six commanderies and ordered archers drawn in the five camps.
translations.idiomatic: He selected Forest Guards from the six commanderies and summoned archers from the five camps.

sentences.zh: 兼折衝而餘勇，鹹重義而輕生。

translations.literal: All could repel the enemy and still had surplus courage; all valued righteousness and held life lightly.
translations.idiomatic: All could repel the foe and still had courage to spare; all valued duty and held life lightly.

sentences.zh: 遂乃因農隙以教民，在春蒐而習戰。

translations.literal: Then he used the agricultural interval to instruct the people and in the spring hunt practiced warfare.
translations.idiomatic: Then he used the farming season's pause to instruct the people and in the spring hunt drilled for war.

sentences.zh: 命司馬以示法，帥掌固而清甸。

translations.literal: He ordered the Minister of War to display the law and the commanders to hold the passes and clear the fields.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the Minister of War to display the law and the commanders to secure the passes and clear the countryside.

sentences.zh: 導旬始以前驅，伏鉤陳而後殿。

translations.literal: He led the Xunshi constellation as vanguard and posted the Gouchén constellation as rear guard.
translations.idiomatic: He led the Xunshi banner as vanguard and posted the Gouchén banner as rear guard.

sentences.zh: 抗鳥旌於析羽，飾魚文於被練。

translations.literal: He raised bird banners on split feathers and adorned fish patterns on quilted armor.
translations.idiomatic: He raised bird banners on plumed staffs and adorned fish-scale patterns on quilted armor.

sentences.zh: 爾乃革軒按轡，玉虯齊鞅。

translations.literal: Then the leather chariot checked the reins and jade dragons aligned the yoke straps.
translations.idiomatic: Then the leather chariot checked its reins and jade dragon fittings lined the yoke.

sentences.zh: 屯左矩以啟行，擊右鐘而傳響。

translations.literal: The left formation halted to begin the march; the right bell was struck and the sound carried.
translations.idiomatic: The left wing halted to begin the march; the right bell was struck and the sound carried far.

sentences.zh: 交雲罕之掩映，紛劍騎而來往。

translations.literal: Cloud canopies crossed in shade and gleam; sword cavalry mingled coming and going.
translations.idiomatic: Cloud canopies crossed in light and shadow; sword cavalry wove back and forth.

sentences.zh: 指攝提於鬥極，洞閶闔之弘敞。

translations.literal: They pointed toward Sheti at the Dipper's pole and pierced the vast breadth of Changhe Gate.
translations.idiomatic: They pointed toward Sheti at the celestial pole and passed the vast breadth of heaven's gate.

sentences.zh: 跨玄武而東臨，款黃山而北上。

translations.literal: They crossed the Black Tortoise and looked east; they approached Mount Huang and went north.
translations.idiomatic: They crossed the Black Tortoise sector and looked east; they approached Mount Huang and marched north.

sentences.zh: 隱圓闕之迢遞，屆方澤之塏爽。

translations.literal: The round watchtower receded in the distance; they arrived at the square marsh's open clarity.
translations.idiomatic: The round watchtower faded in the distance; they reached the square marsh's open ground.

sentences.zh: 于斯時也，青春晚候，朝陽明岫。

translations.literal: At this time, spring's green awaited the evening; the morning sun brightened the peaks.
translations.idiomatic: At this hour spring's green awaited evening; the morning sun lit the mountain peaks.

sentences.zh: 日月光華，煙雲吐秀。

translations.literal: Sun and moon shed splendor; mist and clouds breathed forth elegance.
translations.idiomatic: Sun and moon shed their splendor; mist and clouds breathed forth beauty.

sentences.zh: 澄波瀾于江海，靜氛埃於宇宙。

translations.literal: Waves were cleared on rivers and seas; dust in the cosmos was stilled.
translations.idiomatic: Waves cleared on rivers and seas; dust stilled across the cosmos.

sentences.zh: 乘輿乃禦太一之玉堂，授軍令于紫房。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage then entered the jade hall of the Great One and issued military orders in the purple chamber.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial carriage entered the jade hall of the Great One and issued military orders in the purple chamber.

sentences.zh: 蘊龍韜之妙算，誓武旅於戎場。

translations.literal: He harbored the dragon stratagem's subtle calculations and pledged the martial host on the battlefield.
translations.idiomatic: He harbored the dragon stratagem's subtle plans and pledged the martial host on the field of war.

sentences.zh: 銳金顏於庸蜀，躪鐵騎于漁陽。

translations.literal: He sharpened golden faces at Yong and Shu and trampled iron cavalry at Yuyang.
translations.idiomatic: He honed his warriors in Yong and Shu and trampled iron cavalry at Yuyang.

sentences.zh: 彀神弩而持滿，彏天弧而並張。

translations.literal: He fitted divine crossbows and held them full-drawn; he strung the celestial bow and drew it together.
translations.idiomatic: He fitted divine crossbows and held them at full draw; he strung the celestial bow and drew it taut.

sentences.zh: 曳虹旗之正正，振夔鼓之鏜鏜。

translations.literal: Rainbow banners trailed in ordered ranks; Kui drums were struck with a booming clang.
translations.idiomatic: Rainbow banners trailed in ordered ranks; Kui drums boomed in steady rhythm.

sentences.zh: 八陳肅而成列，六軍儼以相望。

translations.literal: The eight formations stood solemnly in ranks; the six armies looked upon one another in stern array.
translations.idiomatic: The eight formations stood solemnly in ranks; the six armies faced one another in stern array.

sentences.zh: 拒飛梯於縈帶，聳樓車于武岡。

translations.literal: Flying ladders were blocked at the winding belt; siege towers rose on Martial Mound.
translations.idiomatic: Flying ladders were blocked at the winding ramparts; siege towers rose on Martial Mound.

sentences.zh: 或掉鞅而直指，乍交綏而弗傷。

translations.literal: Some loosened the bridle and charged straight; suddenly reins crossed yet no harm was done.
translations.idiomatic: Some loosened the bridle and charged straight ahead; reins crossed in mock combat yet no one was hurt.

sentences.zh: 裁應變而蛇擊，俄蹈厲以鷹揚。

translations.literal: Just adapting to change they struck like serpents; soon treading fiercely they soared like hawks.
translations.idiomatic: Adapting to the moment they struck like serpents; then treading hard they soared like hawks.

sentences.zh: 中小枝於戟刃，徹蹲劄於甲裳。

translations.literal: They hit small branches on halberd blades and pierced squatting targets through armor skirts.
translations.idiomatic: They struck small branches on halberd blades and pierced targets through armor and skirts.

sentences.zh: 聊七縱于孟獲，乃兩擒于卡莊。

translations.literal: For a time they seven times released Meng Huo; then twice captured at Kazhuang.
translations.idiomatic: For a time they released their foe seven times as with Meng Huo; then twice captured him as at Kazhuang.

sentences.zh: 始軒軒而鶴舉，遂離離以雁行。

translations.literal: At first they rose loftily like cranes; then spread apart in goose formation.
translations.idiomatic: At first they rose loftily like cranes; then spread apart in goose formation.

sentences.zh: 振川穀而橫八表，蕩海嶽而耀三光。

translations.literal: They shook valleys and rivers and spanned the eight directions; they swept seas and mountains and gleamed upon the three luminaries.
translations.idiomatic: They shook valleys and rivers and spanned the eight directions; they swept seas and mountains and gleamed upon sun, moon, and stars.

sentences.zh: 諒窈冥之不測，羌進退而難常。

translations.literal: Surely the obscure and unfathomable—how advance and retreat are hard to fix!
translations.idiomatic: Surely the obscure is beyond measure—how advance and retreat are hard to predict!

sentences.zh: 亦有投石扛鼎，超乘挾輈。

translations.literal: There were also stone-throwers and tripod-lifters, leaping onto chariots and seizing the shafts.
translations.idiomatic: There were also men who hurled stones and lifted tripods, leaping onto chariots and seizing the shafts.

sentences.zh: 衝冠聳劍，鐵楯銅頭。

translations.literal: Caps were thrust up and swords raised high; iron shields and bronze helms.
translations.idiomatic: Caps were thrust up and swords raised high; iron shields and bronze helms gleamed.

sentences.zh: 熊渠殆凶，武勇操牛。

translations.literal: Xiong Qu was nearly deadly; Wu Yong grasped oxen.
translations.idiomatic: Men fierce as Xiong Qu were nearly deadly; men bold as Wu Yong could seize oxen.

sentences.zh: 雖任鄙與賁、育，故無得而為仇。

translations.literal: Though there were Ren Zhi and Ben and Yu, still none could become their foe.
translations.idiomatic: Though warriors rivaled Ren Zhi, Ben Bo, and Xia Yu, none could stand as their foe.

sentences.zh: 九攻既決，三略已周。

translations.literal: The nine assaults were decided; the three strategies completed.
translations.idiomatic: The nine assaults were decided; the three strategies were complete.

sentences.zh: 鳴鐲振響，風卷電收。

translations.literal: Bells rang and sounds shook; wind rolled up and lightning withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Bells rang and sounds shook; wind rolled up and lightning faded.

sentences.zh: 於是勇爵班，金奏設，登元、凱而陪位，命方、邵而就列。

translations.literal: Thereupon brave ranks were distributed, golden music was set up; Yuan and Kai ascended to attendant seats; Fang and Shao were ordered to take their places.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon brave ranks were awarded, golden music was played; the foremost heroes took their seats; Fang and Shao were ordered into the ranks.

sentences.zh: 三獻式序，八音未闋。

translations.literal: The three offerings proceeded in order; the eight sounds had not ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The three offerings proceeded in order; the eight instruments had not yet ceased.

sentences.zh: 舞干戚而有豫，聽鼓鞞而載悅。

translations.literal: They danced with shields and axes in delight; hearing drums and hand-drums they were filled with joy.
translations.idiomatic: They danced with shields and axes in delight; hearing drums and hand-drums they were filled with joy.

sentences.zh: 俾挾纊與投醪，鹹忘軀而殉節。

translations.literal: They were made to share cotton garments and cast wine; all forgot their bodies and died for duty.
translations.idiomatic: They shared warm garments and cast wine to one another; all forgot their bodies and died for duty.

sentences.zh: 方席捲而橫行，見王師之有征。

translations.literal: Just as mats were rolled and they marched across, one saw the royal army had a campaign.
translations.idiomatic: As mats were rolled and they marched across the land, one saw the royal army go forth to war.

sentences.zh: 登燕山而戮封豕，臨瀚海而斬長鯨。

translations.literal: They ascended Mount Yan and slew the sealed boar; they came to the vast sea and cut the long whale.
translations.idiomatic: They ascended Mount Yan and slew the great boar; they came to the vast sea and cut down the long whale.

sentences.zh: 望雲亭而載蹕，禮升中而告成。

translations.literal: They gazed at Cloud Pavilion and halted the imperial train; they performed the rite of ascending the central peak and announced completion.
translations.idiomatic: They gazed at Cloud Pavilion and halted the imperial train; they performed the rite on the central peak and announced success.

sentences.zh: 實皇王之神武，信蕩蕩而難名者也。

translations.literal: Truly the divine martial power of the emperor-king—surely vast and hard to name!
translations.idiomatic: Truly this is the divine martial power of the emperor—vast beyond naming!

sentences.zh: 陳主嘉之，賜馬一匹。

translations.literal: The Chen ruler praised it and bestowed one horse.
translations.idiomatic: The Chen emperor praised it and rewarded him with a horse.

sentences.zh: 及陳滅歸國，為通直郎，直內史省。

translations.literal: When Chen fell he returned to his state and became General Communication Attendant, serving in the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen fell he returned home and became General Communication Attendant, serving in the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 貧無產業，每傭書養親，怏怏不平。

translations.literal: Poor without property, he often copied books to support his parents, resentful and discontent.
translations.idiomatic: Poor and without property, he often copied books for hire to support his parents, brooding with discontent.

sentences.zh: 嘗為五言詩以見意，情理淒切，世以為工，作者莫不吟詠。

translations.literal: He once composed pentasyllabic verse to express his feelings; the sentiment was poignant and the world considered it skilled, and writers all chanted it.
translations.idiomatic: He once wrote pentasyllabic verse to express his feelings; the emotion was poignant, contemporaries judged it masterly, and poets everywhere recited it.

sentences.zh: 未幾，拜內史舍人。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Secretariat Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed Secretariat Attendant.

sentences.zh: 煬帝即位，顧遇彌隆。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang took the throne, his favor grew ever greater.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang took the throne, his favor grew ever greater.

sentences.zh: 禮書監河東柳顧言博學有才，罕所推謝，至是與世基相見，歎曰：「海內當共推此一人，非吾儕所及也。

translations.literal: Director of Rites Liu Guyan of Hedong was broadly learned and talented and rarely praised or deferred to others; now he met Shiji and sighed: "Within the seas this one man should be jointly acclaimed; he is not what our sort can match.
translations.idiomatic: Director of Rites Liu Guyan of Hedong was learned and talented and rarely praised anyone; when he met Shiji he sighed and said, "Within the empire this one man alone deserves universal acclaim; none of us can match him.

sentences.zh: 」俄遷內史侍郎，以母憂去職，哀毀骨立。

translations.literal: " Soon he was transferred to Vice Director of the Secretariat; on his mother's death he left office, his mourning so extreme that only skin and bone remained.
translations.idiomatic: " Soon he was promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat; when his mother died he left office, mourning so grievously that he was skin and bone.

sentences.zh: 有詔起令視事，拜見之日，殆不能起，帝令左右扶之。

translations.literal: An edict recalled him to resume duties; on the day he came to audience he could scarcely rise, and the emperor ordered attendants to support him.
translations.idiomatic: An edict recalled him to duty; on the day he came to audience he could scarcely stand, and the emperor ordered attendants to support him.

sentences.zh: 哀其羸瘠，詔令進肉，世基食輒悲哽，不能下。

translations.literal: Pitying his emaciation, the emperor ordered meat brought; Shiji ate and at once choked with grief, unable to swallow.
translations.idiomatic: Pitying his emaciation, the emperor ordered meat served; Shiji ate and at once choked with grief, unable to swallow.

sentences.zh: 帝使謂之曰：「方相委任，當為國惜身。

translations.literal: The emperor sent someone to tell him: "I am just now entrusting you with duties; you should spare your body for the state.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent word: "I am entrusting you with great responsibility; you must spare your strength for the state.

sentences.zh: 」前後敦勸者數矣。

translations.literal: " He urged him thus several times.
translations.idiomatic: " He urged him thus several times.

sentences.zh: 帝重其才，親禮逾厚，專典機密，與納言蘇威、左翊衛大將軍宇文述、黃門侍郎裴矩、御史大夫裴蘊等參掌朝政。

translations.literal: The emperor valued his talent, his personal courtesy grew ever thicker, and he was put in sole charge of confidential matters; with Supplicator Su Wei, Left Guard General Yuwen Shu, Yellow Gate Attendant Pei Ju, Censor-in-Chief Pei Yun, and others he jointly managed court government.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor valued his talent and treated him with ever greater personal regard, entrusting him with confidential affairs; with Su Wei, Yuwen Shu, Pei Ju, Pei Yun, and others he jointly directed the government.

sentences.zh: 于時天下多事，四方表奏日有百數。

translations.literal: At that time the realm had many troubles; memorials from the four directions numbered in the hundreds each day.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the realm was in turmoil; memorials from every quarter numbered in the hundreds each day.

sentences.zh: 帝方凝重，事不庭決，入閤之後，始召世基口授節度。

translations.literal: The emperor was then grave and weighty; matters were not decided in open court; after entering the inner chambers he would summon Shiji and dictate instructions orally.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was grave and deliberate; matters were not decided in open court; after entering the inner chambers he would summon Shiji and dictate his instructions orally.

sentences.zh: 世基至省，方為敕書，日且百紙，無所遺謬。

translations.literal: Shiji would go to the secretariat and then draft edicts; nearly a hundred sheets a day, with nothing omitted or in error.
translations.idiomatic: Shiji would go to the secretariat and draft the edicts—nearly a hundred documents a day, without omission or error.

sentences.zh: 其精審如是。

translations.literal: His precision and care were such as this.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his precision and care.

sentences.zh: 遼東之役，進位金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: During the Liaodong campaign he was advanced to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: During the Liaodong campaign he was promoted to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.

sentences.zh: 後從幸雁門，帝為突厥所圍，戰士多敗。

translations.literal: Later he followed the emperor to Yanmen; the emperor was surrounded by the Turks and many soldiers were defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Later he accompanied the emperor to Yanmen; the emperor was surrounded by the Turks and many soldiers were defeated.

sentences.zh: 世基勸帝重為賞格，親自撫循，又下詔停遼東之事。

translations.literal: Shiji urged the emperor to renew reward standards, personally comfort the troops, and also issue an edict halting the Liaodong campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Shiji urged the emperor to renew the reward standards, personally comfort the troops, and issue an edict halting the Liaodong campaign.

sentences.zh: 帝從之，師乃複振。

translations.literal: The emperor followed his advice and the army was thereby revived.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor followed his advice and the army's morale revived.

sentences.zh: 及圍解，勳格不行，又下伐遼之詔。

translations.literal: When the siege was lifted, the merit standards were not carried out, and another edict was issued to attack Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: When the siege was lifted, the promised rewards were not granted, and another edict was issued to attack Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 由是言其詐眾，朝野離心。

translations.literal: Because of this people said he deceived the masses, and court and countryside lost heart.
translations.idiomatic: Because of this people said he had deceived the masses, and court and countryside alike lost faith in him.

sentences.zh: 帝幸江都，次鞏縣，世基以盜賊日盛，請發兵屯洛口倉，以備不虞。

translations.literal: The emperor went to Jiangdu and halted at Gong County; Shiji, because bandits grew daily, requested troops be sent to garrison the Luokou granary against the unexpected.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor went to Jiangdu and halted at Gong County; as banditry grew daily, Shiji requested troops to garrison the Luokou granary against surprise attack.

sentences.zh: 帝不從，但答雲：「卿是書生，定猶恇怯。

translations.literal: The emperor did not agree but only answered: "You are a bookish man and surely still timid and fearful.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused and only replied, "You are a scholar and surely still timid and fearful.

sentences.zh: 」于時天下大亂，世基知帝不可諫止，又以高熲、張衡等相繼誅戮，懼禍及己，雖居近侍，唯諾取容，不敢忤意。

translations.literal: " At that time the realm was in great disorder; Shiji knew the emperor could not be remonstrated with and stopped, and moreover because Gao Jiong, Zhang Heng, and others were executed one after another, he feared disaster would reach himself; though he served close at hand, he only assented to please and did not dare oppose the emperor's will.
translations.idiomatic: " The realm was in chaos; Shiji knew the emperor could not be dissuaded, and with Gao Jiong, Zhang Heng, and others executed one after another, he feared for his own life; though he served at the emperor's side, he only assented and dared not oppose him.

sentences.zh: 盜賊日甚，郡縣多沒。

translations.literal: Bandits grew worse day by day and many commanderies and counties fell.
translations.idiomatic: Banditry grew worse daily and many commanderies and counties fell.

sentences.zh: 世基知帝惡數聞之，後有告敗者，乃抑損表狀，不以實聞。

translations.literal: Shiji knew the emperor hated hearing such news repeatedly; afterward when there were reports of defeat he would reduce and diminish the memorials and not report the facts.
translations.idiomatic: Shiji knew the emperor hated repeated bad news; when reports of defeat arrived he would tone down the memorials and not report the full truth.

sentences.zh: 是後外間有變，帝弗之知也。

translations.literal: After this when there were changes outside, the emperor did not know of them.
translations.idiomatic: After this, when trouble arose in the provinces, the emperor knew nothing of it.

sentences.zh: 嘗遣太僕楊義臣捕盜于河北，降賊數十萬，列狀上聞。

translations.literal: He once sent Grand Master of the Stud Yang Yichen to capture bandits in Hebei; he subdued several hundred thousand rebels and submitted a detailed report.
translations.idiomatic: He once sent Yang Yichen to suppress bandits in Hebei; Yichen subdued several hundred thousand rebels and submitted a detailed report.

sentences.zh: 帝歎曰：「我初不聞賊頓如此，義臣降賊何多也！

translations.literal: The emperor sighed and said: "I had not heard at first that bandits were suddenly like this—how many rebels has Yichen subdued!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sighed and said, "I had not realized banditry had grown so severe—how many rebels has Yichen subdued!

sentences.zh: 」世基對曰：「鼠竊雖多，未足為慮。

translations.literal: " Shiji replied: "Though petty thieves are many, they are not worth concern.
translations.idiomatic: " Shiji replied, "Though petty thieves are many, they are not worth concern.

sentences.zh: 義臣克之，擁兵不少，久在閫外，此最非宜。

translations.literal: Yichen has subdued them but holds no small army and has long been outside the capital—this is most improper.
translations.idiomatic: Yichen has defeated them but commands a large force and has long been outside the capital—this is most improper.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「卿言是也。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "Your words are right.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "You are right.

sentences.zh: 」遽追義臣，放其兵散。

translations.literal: " He hastily recalled Yichen and dispersed his troops.
translations.idiomatic: " He hastily recalled Yichen and dispersed his troops.

sentences.zh: 又越王侗遣太常丞元善達間行賊中，詣江都奏事，稱李密有眾百萬，圍逼京都，賊據洛口倉，城內無食，若陛下速還，烏合必散，不然者，東都決沒。

translations.literal: Also Prince of Yue Yang Tong sent Director of Sacrifices Yuan Shanda by secret route through the bandits to Jiangdu to report: he said Li Mi had a force of a million, besieging the capital; the rebels held the Luokou granary and the city within had no food; if Your Majesty returned quickly the rabble would surely scatter, otherwise the eastern capital would certainly fall.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Yue also sent Yuan Shanda by secret route through rebel territory to Jiangdu to report that Li Mi commanded a million men and was besieging the eastern capital; the rebels held the Luokou granary and the city had no food; if the emperor returned quickly the rabble would scatter, otherwise the eastern capital would surely fall.

sentences.zh: 因歔欷嗚咽，帝為之改容。

translations.literal: He thereupon sobbed and wept, and the emperor's expression changed for him.
translations.idiomatic: He sobbed and wept, and the emperor's expression changed.

sentences.zh: 世基見帝色憂，進曰：「越王年小，此輩誑之。

translations.literal: Shiji saw the emperor's worried look and advanced, saying: "The Prince of Yue is young; these people deceive him.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the emperor's worried look, Shiji stepped forward and said, "The Prince of Yue is young; these people are deceiving him.

sentences.zh: 若如所言，善達何緣來至？

translations.literal: If it were as they say, by what means did Shanda come here?
translations.idiomatic: If things were as they say, how could Shanda have reached here at all?

sentences.zh: 」帝乃勃然怒曰：「善達小人，敢廷辱我！

translations.literal: " The emperor then flared in anger and said: "Shanda is a petty man who dares insult me in court!
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor flared with anger and said, "Shanda is a petty man who dares insult me in open court!

sentences.zh: 」因使經賊中，向東陽催運，善達遂為群盜所殺。

translations.literal: " He therefore sent him through the bandit territory to Dongyang to urge transport, and Shanda was thereupon killed by the bandit hosts.
translations.idiomatic: " He sent him back through rebel territory to Dongyang to urge grain transport, and Shanda was killed by the bandits.

sentences.zh: 此後外人杜口，莫敢以賊聞奏。

translations.literal: After this outsiders kept silent and none dared report bandits in memorials.
translations.idiomatic: After this no one outside dared report bandit activity in memorials.

sentences.zh: 世基貌沉審，言多合意，是以特見親愛，朝臣無與為比。

translations.literal: Shiji's appearance was deep and composed and his words mostly matched the emperor's intent; therefore he was especially beloved, and no court minister could be compared with him.
translations.idiomatic: Shiji was grave in manner and his words usually pleased the emperor; he was especially favored, and no court minister could compare with him.

sentences.zh: 其繼室孫氏，性驕淫，世基惑之，恣其奢靡。

translations.literal: His second wife, the Sun clan, was by nature proud and dissolute; Shiji was infatuated with her and indulged her extravagance.
translations.idiomatic: His second wife, Lady Sun, was proud and dissolute; infatuated with her, Shiji indulged her extravagance.

sentences.zh: 雕飾器服，無複素士之風。

translations.literal: Carved and adorned vessels and dress—no longer the manner of a plain scholar.
translations.idiomatic: Their vessels and dress were lavishly ornamented, far from the manner of a plain scholar.

sentences.zh: 孫複攜前夫子夏侯儼入世基舍，而頑鄙無賴，為其聚斂。

translations.literal: Sun also brought her former husband's son Xiahou Yan into Shiji's household; he was obstinate, base, and worthless and amassed wealth for them.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Sun also brought her former husband's son Xiahou Yan into Shiji's household; coarse and worthless, he amassed wealth for them.

sentences.zh: 鬻官賣獄，賄賂公行，其門如市，金寶盈積。

translations.literal: They sold offices and sold judgments; bribes were openly practiced; their gate was like a market and gold and jewels piled up.
translations.idiomatic: They sold offices and judgments; bribes flowed openly; their gate was like a market and gold and jewels piled high.

sentences.zh: 其弟世南，素國士，而清貧不立，未曾有所贍。

translations.literal: His younger brother Shinan was by nature a man of the state but poor and upright without establishment; Shiji had never given him support.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Shinan was a man of integrity but poor and unsupported; Shiji never gave him anything.

sentences.zh: 由是為論者所譏，朝野鹹共疾怨。

translations.literal: Because of this he was mocked by critics, and court and countryside alike hated and resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Because of this critics mocked him, and court and countryside alike hated and resented him.

sentences.zh: 宇文化及殺逆也，世基乃見害焉。

translations.literal: When Yuwen Huaji committed regicide, Shiji was thereupon killed.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuwen Huaji murdered the emperor, Shiji was killed as well.

sentences.zh: 長子肅，好學多才藝，時人稱有家風。

translations.literal: His eldest son Su was fond of learning and had many talents; contemporaries praised the family's tradition.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Su was studious and talented; contemporaries praised the family's tradition.

sentences.zh: 弱冠早沒。

translations.literal: He died young before his prime.
translations.idiomatic: He died young before reaching his prime.

sentences.zh: 肅弟熙，大業末為符璽郎。

translations.literal: Su's younger brother Xi, at the end of the Daye era, was Seal and Credential Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Su's younger brother Xi served as Seal and Credential Attendant at the end of the Daye era.

sentences.zh: 次子柔、晦，並宣義郎。

translations.literal: The second sons Rou and Hui were both Gentlemen for Spreading Righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: The second sons Rou and Hui were both Gentlemen for Spreading Righteousness.

sentences.zh: 化及將亂之夕，宗人虞伋知而告熙曰：「事勢以然，吾將濟卿南渡，且得免禍，同死何益！

translations.literal: On the eve of Huaji's rebellion, his clansman Yu Ji knew of it and told Xi: "Events have come to this; I will ferry you south across the river so you may escape disaster—what use is dying together!
translations.idiomatic: On the eve of Huaji's rebellion, his clansman Yu Ji learned of it and told Xi, "Events have come to this; I will ferry you south across the river so you may escape—what use is dying together!

sentences.zh: 」熙謂伋曰：「棄父背君，求生何地？

translations.literal: " Xi said to Ji: "Abandoning one's father and turning against one's lord—where is there a place to seek life?
translations.idiomatic: " Xi said to Ji, "Abandoning one's father and turning against one's lord—where could one seek life?

sentences.zh: 感尊之懷，自此訣矣。

translations.literal: Touched by your generous feeling, from this we take leave.
translations.idiomatic: I am touched by your kindness, but from this we part forever.

sentences.zh: 」及難作，兄弟競請先死，行刑人於是先世基殺之。

translations.literal: " When disaster struck, the brothers competed to die first; the executioners therefore killed Shiji first and then them.
translations.idiomatic: " When disaster struck, the brothers competed to die first; the executioners killed Shiji first, then them.

sentences.zh: 裴蘊，河東聞喜人也。

translations.literal: Pei Yun was a native of Wenxi in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Yun came from Wenxi in Hedong.

sentences.zh: 祖之平，梁衛將軍。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zhiping was a Wei general of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhiping was a guard general of Liang.

sentences.zh: 父忌，陳都官尚書，與吳明徹同沒于周，賜爵江夏郡公，在隋十餘年而卒。

translations.literal: His father Ji was Director of the Ministry of Justice in Chen; he perished together with Wu Mingche in Zhou territory and was granted the title Duke of Jiangxia; he lived in Sui more than ten years and then died.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ji was Director of the Ministry of Justice under Chen; he was captured with Wu Mingche by Northern Zhou and ennobled as Duke of Jiangxia; he lived in Sui more than ten years before his death.

sentences.zh: 蘊性明辯，有吏幹。

translations.literal: Yun was by nature clear and argumentative and had administrative ability.
translations.idiomatic: Yun was sharp and articulate and had strong administrative ability.

sentences.zh: 在陳仕曆直閣將軍、興甯令。

translations.literal: In Chen service he passed through the posts of Direct Gate General and Magistrate of Xingning.
translations.idiomatic: Under Chen he served as Direct Gate General and magistrate of Xingning.

sentences.zh: 蘊以其父在北，陰奉表于高祖，請為內應。

translations.literal: Yun, because his father was in the north, secretly submitted a memorial to Emperor Gaozu requesting to serve as an inside agent.
translations.idiomatic: Because his father was in the north, Yun secretly submitted a memorial to Emperor Gaozu offering to serve as an inside agent.

sentences.zh: 及陳平，上悉閱江南衣冠之士，次至蘊，上以為夙有向化之心，超授儀同。

translations.literal: When Chen was pacified, the emperor reviewed all the gentry scholars of the south in turn; when it came to Yun, the emperor thought he had long had a heart turned toward transformation and exceptionally granted him Palace Attendant rank.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen fell, the emperor reviewed the southern gentry in turn; when he reached Yun, believing Yun had long wished to submit, he exceptionally granted him Palace Attendant rank.

sentences.zh: 左僕射高熲不悟上旨，進諫曰：「裴蘊無功于國，寵逾倫輩，臣未見其可。

translations.literal: Left Vice Director Gao Jiong did not grasp the emperor's intent and advanced a remonstrance, saying: "Pei Yun has no merit to the state; his favor exceeds his peers—I do not see how this is acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: Left Vice Director Gao Jiong did not grasp the emperor's intent and remonstrated, "Pei Yun has rendered no service to the state; his favor exceeds his peers—I do not see how this is justified.

sentences.zh: 」上又加蘊上儀同，熲複進諫，上曰：「可加開府。

translations.literal: " The emperor further raised Yun to Senior Palace Attendant; Jiong again remonstrated; the emperor said: "He may be made Opening the Government.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor further promoted Yun to Senior Palace Attendant; Jiong remonstrated again; the emperor said, "Then make him Opening the Government.

sentences.zh: 」熲乃不敢複言，即日拜開府儀同三司，禮賜優洽。

translations.literal: " Jiong then dared not speak again; that same day Yun was appointed Grand Master of the Palace with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, Third Class, with generous ritual gifts.
translations.idiomatic: " Jiong dared speak no further; that same day Yun was appointed Grand Master of the Palace with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, Third Class, with generous gifts.

sentences.zh: 曆洋、直、隸三州刺史，俱有能名。

translations.literal: He passed through the three prefectures of Yang, Zhi, and Ji as governor, all with a reputation for ability.
translations.idiomatic: He served as governor of Yang, Zhi, and Ji prefectures, earning a reputation for ability in each.

sentences.zh: 大業初，考績連最。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Daye, his performance evaluations were repeatedly top-ranked.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Daye era, his performance evaluations were repeatedly top-ranked.

sentences.zh: 煬帝聞其善政，征為太常少卿。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang heard of his good governance and summoned him as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang heard of his good governance and summoned him as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 初，高祖不好聲技，遣牛弘定樂，非正聲清商及九部四儛之色，皆罷遣從民。

translations.literal: Earlier, Emperor Gaozu did not favor music and performing arts; he sent Niu Hong to fix the music; all that was not orthodox sound, clear shang mode, or the colors of the nine departments and four dances was dismissed and returned to the people.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Emperor Gaozu disliked music and entertainments; he sent Niu Hong to regulate music and dismissed all non-orthodox sounds, clear shang melodies, and the nine departments' four dances, returning performers to the populace.

sentences.zh: 至是，蘊揣知帝意，奏括天下周、齊、梁、陳樂家子弟，皆為樂戶。

translations.literal: By this time Yun guessed the emperor's intent and memorialized to gather the music-house sons and younger brothers of Zhou, Qi, Liang, and Chen throughout the realm, all making them music households.
translations.idiomatic: By then Yun guessed the emperor's intent and memorialized to register music-house descendants from Zhou, Qi, Liang, and Chen throughout the realm as music households.

sentences.zh: 其六品已下，至於民庶，有善音樂及倡優百戲者，皆直太常。

translations.literal: Those of sixth rank and below down to common people who were skilled in music or were singers, actors, and hundred entertainments—all were assigned to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Those of sixth rank and below, down to commoners skilled in music or in singing, acting, and variety entertainments, were all assigned to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 是後異技淫聲鹹萃樂府，皆置博士弟子，遞相教傳，增益樂人至三萬餘。

translations.literal: After this exotic skills and licentious sounds all gathered in the Music Bureau; doctorate students were all established, teaching one another in succession, increasing musicians to more than thirty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter exotic skills and licentious music all gathered in the Music Bureau; doctorate students were appointed to teach one another, and musicians increased to more than thirty thousand.

sentences.zh: 帝大悅，遷民部侍郎。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and transferred him to Vice Director of the Ministry of Population.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased and promoted him to Vice Director of the Ministry of Population.

sentences.zh: 于時猶承高祖和平之後，禁網疏闊，戶口多漏。

translations.literal: At that time they still inherited the peace after Emperor Gaozu; prohibitions were lax and household registers had many omissions.
translations.idiomatic: The realm still enjoyed the peace left by Emperor Gaozu; regulations were lax and household registers had many omissions.

sentences.zh: 或年及成丁，猶詐為小，未至於老，已免租賦。

translations.literal: Some who had reached adult age still falsely claimed to be young; some not yet old were already exempted from rent and tax.
translations.idiomatic: Some who had reached adulthood still falsely claimed to be minors; some not yet old were already exempt from rent and tax.

sentences.zh: 蘊曆為刺史，素知其情，因是條奏，皆令貌閱。

translations.literal: Yun had served repeatedly as prefectural governor and long knew these circumstances; he therefore submitted a detailed memorial ordering all to be inspected by appearance.
translations.idiomatic: Yun had served repeatedly as prefectural governor and knew these abuses well; he therefore memorialized ordering physical inspection of all registrants.

sentences.zh: 若一人不實，則官司解職，鄉正裡長皆遠流配。

translations.literal: If even one person was not genuine, the office was dismissed from post and the village head and hamlet chief were all exiled to distant places.
translations.idiomatic: If even one registrant was found false, the responsible officials were dismissed and village and hamlet heads were exiled.

sentences.zh: 又許民相告，若糾得一丁者，令被糾之家代輸賦役。

translations.literal: He also allowed the people to inform on one another; if one adult male was reported, the reported household was made to pay his rent and corvée in his stead.
translations.idiomatic: He also allowed mutual denunciation; if one concealed adult male was reported, the reported household had to pay his taxes and corvée.

sentences.zh: 是歲大業五年也，諸郡計帳，進丁二十四萬三千，新附口六十四萬一千五百。

translations.literal: That year was the fifth year of Daye; the commanderies' census accounts added 243,000 adult males and 641,500 newly registered dependents.
translations.idiomatic: That year, the fifth year of Daye, the commanderies' census accounts reported 243,000 new adult males and 641,500 newly registered dependents.

sentences.zh: 帝臨朝覽狀，謂百官曰：「前代無好人，致此罔冒。

translations.literal: The emperor faced court and reviewed the reports, telling the hundred officials: "Former ages had no good men, leading to this fraud and falsehood.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor reviewed the reports in court and told the officials, "Former ages had no capable men, which led to this widespread fraud.

sentences.zh: 今進民戶口皆從實者，全由裴蘊一人用心。

translations.literal: Now the registered population submitted is all according to fact—entirely through Pei Yun's single-minded effort.
translations.idiomatic: That the registered population is now accurate is entirely due to Pei Yun's devoted effort alone.

sentences.zh: 古語雲，得賢而治，驗之信矣。

translations.literal: The old saying says: obtain the worthy and the realm is governed—verified, this is true!
translations.idiomatic: The old saying holds that finding the worthy brings good government—here the truth of it is proved!

sentences.zh: 」由是漸見親委，拜京兆贊治，發擿纖毫，吏民懾憚。

translations.literal: " From this he was gradually entrusted with intimacy, appointed Assistant Administrator of Jingzhao, exposing matters down to the finest thread; officials and people were in awe and fear.
translations.idiomatic: " From this he was gradually entrusted with greater responsibility, appointed Assistant Administrator of Jingzhao; he exposed every detail and officials and commoners alike feared him.

sentences.zh: 未幾，擢授御史大夫，與裴矩、虞世基參掌機密。

translations.literal: Before long he was promoted and appointed Censor-in-Chief, and with Pei Ju and Yu Shiji jointly managed confidential affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was promoted to Censor-in-Chief and with Pei Ju and Yu Shiji jointly managed confidential affairs.

sentences.zh: 蘊善候伺人主微意，若欲罪者，則曲法順情，鍛成其罪。

translations.literal: Yun was skilled at watching for the ruler's subtle intent; if the emperor wished to punish someone, he would bend the law to suit feeling and forge the crime.
translations.idiomatic: Yun was skilled at reading the emperor's subtle intent; when the emperor wished to punish someone, he would bend the law and forge the case.

sentences.zh: 所欲宥者，則附從輕典，因而釋之。

translations.literal: Those the emperor wished to pardon he would attach to lenient statutes and thereby release.
translations.idiomatic: Those the emperor wished to pardon he would attach to lenient statutes and release.

sentences.zh: 是後大小之獄皆以付蘊，憲部大理莫敢與奪，必稟承進止，然後決斷。

translations.literal: After this great and small cases were all entrusted to Yun; the Ministry of Justice and Court of Review dared not dispute; they had to report and receive instructions before deciding.
translations.idiomatic: After this all cases great and small were entrusted to Yun; the Ministry of Justice and Court of Review dared not override him; they had to await his instructions before deciding.

sentences.zh: 蘊亦機辯，所論法理，言若懸河，或重或輕，皆由其口，剖析明敏，時人不能致詰。

translations.literal: Yun was also quick and argumentative; in discussing law and principle his words were like a hanging river; whether heavy or light, all came from his mouth; his analysis was clear and sharp, and contemporaries could not cross-examine him.
translations.idiomatic: Yun was also quick-witted; in legal argument his words flowed like a river; whether the penalty was heavy or light came from his mouth alone; his analysis was sharp, and no one could refute him.

sentences.zh: 楊玄感之反也，帝遣蘊推其黨與，謂蘊曰：「玄感一呼而從者十萬，益知天下人不欲多，多即相聚為盜耳。

translations.literal: When Yang Xuangan rebelled, the emperor sent Yun to investigate his associates and told Yun: "Xuangan gave one call and a hundred thousand followed—this further shows the people of the realm do not want many; when there are many they gather and become bandits.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Xuangan rebelled, the emperor sent Yun to investigate his associates and told him, "Xuangan gave one call and a hundred thousand followed—this shows the people do not want large numbers; when too many gather they become bandits.

sentences.zh: 不盡加誅，則後無以勸。

translations.literal: If we do not execute them all, afterward there will be no means to encourage obedience.
translations.idiomatic: Unless we execute them all, there will be no deterring others afterward.

sentences.zh: 」蘊由是乃峻法治之，所戮者數萬人，皆籍沒其家。

translations.literal: " Yun therefore applied severe law in the case; those executed numbered in the tens of thousands, and all their households were registered and confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: " Yun therefore applied harsh justice; tens of thousands were executed and their families' property confiscated.

sentences.zh: 帝大稱善，賜奴婢十五口。

translations.literal: The emperor greatly praised this as good and bestowed fifteen male and female servants.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor greatly praised him and bestowed fifteen servants.

sentences.zh: 司隸大夫薛道衡以忤意獲譴，蘊知帝惡之，乃奏曰：「道衡負才恃舊，有無君之心。

translations.literal: Director of the Capital Xue Daoheng was punished for offending the emperor's intent; Yun knew the emperor hated him and memorialized: "Daoheng relies on talent and presumes on old association; he has a heart without a ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Capital Xue Daoheng was punished for offending the emperor; Yun knew the emperor hated him and memorialized, "Daoheng relies on his talent and old association; he harbors disloyal thoughts.

sentences.zh: 見詔書每下，便腹非私議，推惡于國，妄造禍端。

translations.literal: Whenever he saw an edict issued he would privately criticize it in his belly, pushing blame onto the state and recklessly creating sources of disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever an edict was issued he privately criticized it, blaming the state and recklessly stirring trouble.

sentences.zh: 論其罪名，似如隱昧，源其情意，深為悖逆。

translations.literal: Judging his criminal name, it seems obscure; tracing the source of his intent and feeling, it is deeply rebellious.
translations.idiomatic: Judging by the letter of the law his offense seems obscure, but tracing his intent it is deeply rebellious.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「然。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "So.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "Exactly.

sentences.zh: 我少時與此人相隨行役，輕我童稚，共高熲、賀若弼等外擅威權，自知罪當誣惣。

translations.literal: When I was young I followed this man on campaigns; he looked down on my youth; together with Gao Jiong, He Ruo Bi, and others he arrogated authority outside, and knew himself guilty and deserving of false accusation.
translations.idiomatic: When I was young I campaigned with this man; he looked down on my youth; together with Gao Jiong, He Ruo Bi, and others he arrogated power, and knew himself guilty.

sentences.zh: 及我即位，懷不自安，賴天下無事，未得反耳。

translations.literal: When I took the throne he felt ill at ease; relying on the realm being without trouble, he had not yet been able to rebel.
translations.idiomatic: When I took the throne he felt uneasy; only because the realm was at peace had he not yet rebelled.

sentences.zh: 公論其逆，妙體本心。

translations.literal: You discuss his rebellion and wonderfully embody my inner heart.
translations.idiomatic: Your account of his treason perfectly captures what I have long felt.

sentences.zh: 」於是誅道衡。

translations.literal: " Daoheng was thereupon executed.
translations.idiomatic: " Daoheng was thereupon executed.

sentences.zh: 又帝問蘇威以討遼之策，威不願帝複行，且欲令帝知天下多賊，乃詭答曰：「今者之役，不願發兵，但詔赦群盜，自可得數十萬。

translations.literal: Also the emperor asked Su Wei about the strategy for attacking Liaodong; Wei did not wish the emperor to campaign again and moreover wanted the emperor to know the realm had many bandits; he therefore answered deceitfully: "For the present campaign, I do not wish to send troops; only issue an edict pardoning the bandit hosts and you will naturally obtain several hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also asked Su Wei about the strategy for attacking Liaodong; Wei did not want the emperor to campaign again and wished him to know how many bandits filled the realm; he answered evasively, "For this campaign I would not send troops; only issue an edict pardoning the bandit hosts and you will naturally gain several hundred thousand men.

sentences.zh: 遣關內奴賊及山東曆山飛、張金稱等頭別為一軍，出遼西道，諸河南賊王薄、孟讓等十餘頭並給舟楫，浮滄海道，必喜於免罪，競務立功，一歲之間，可滅高麗矣。

translations.literal: Send the Guanzhong slave-bandits and the Shandong leaders Lishan Fei, Zhang Jincheng, and others as a separate army by the Liaoxi route; give boats to the more than ten Henan bandit leaders Wang Bo, Meng Rang, and the rest to sail the Canghai route—they will surely rejoice at pardon and compete to achieve merit; within one year Goguryeo can be destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Send the Guanzhong slave-bandits and Shandong leaders such as Lishan Fei and Zhang Jincheng as a separate army along the Liaoxi route; equip the dozen-odd Henan bandit chiefs Wang Bo, Meng Rang, and others with boats to sail the eastern sea route—they will rejoice at pardon and compete for merit; within a year Goguryeo can be destroyed.

sentences.zh: 」帝不懌曰：「我去尚猶未克，鼠竊安能濟乎？

translations.literal: " The emperor displeased said: "When I go I still have not conquered them—how can petty thieves succeed?
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said displeased, "When I go I still cannot conquer them—how can petty thieves succeed?

sentences.zh: 」威出後，蘊奏曰：「此大不遜，天下何處有許多賊！

translations.literal: " After Wei left, Yun memorialized: "This is greatly insubordinate—where in the realm are there so many bandits!
translations.idiomatic: " After Wei left, Yun memorialized, "This is grossly insubordinate—where in the realm are there so many bandits!

sentences.zh: 」帝悟曰：「老革多奸，將賊脅我。

translations.literal: " The emperor understood and said: "The old fellow is full of treachery; he uses bandits to threaten me.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor understood and said, "The old man is full of treachery; he uses bandits to threaten me.

sentences.zh: 欲搭其口，但隱忍之，誠極難耐。

translations.literal: I want to shut his mouth but only bear it in silence—truly extremely hard to endure.
translations.idiomatic: I want to shut his mouth but can only bear it in silence—it is truly unbearable.

sentences.zh: 」蘊知上意，遣張行本奏威罪惡，帝付蘊推鞫之，乃處其死。

translations.literal: " Yun knew the emperor's intent and sent Zhang Xingben to memorialize Wei's crimes; the emperor entrusted Yun to investigate and interrogate him, and thus arranged his death.
translations.idiomatic: " Yun knew the emperor's intent and had Zhang Xingben memorialize Wei's crimes; the emperor entrusted Yun to investigate him and arranged his execution.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「未忍便殺。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "I cannot yet bear to kill him outright.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I cannot yet bear to kill him outright.

sentences.zh: 」遂父子及孫三世並除名。

translations.literal: " Thereupon father and son and three generations of grandsons were all struck from the registers.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon father, son, and three generations of descendants were all struck from the registers.

sentences.zh: 蘊又欲重己權勢，令虞世基奏罷司隸刺史以下官屬，增置禦史百餘人。

translations.literal: Yun also wished to increase his own power and authority, and had Yu Shiji memorialize to abolish the subordinate officials from Director of the Capital down and add more than a hundred censors.
translations.idiomatic: Yun also wished to increase his power and had Yu Shiji memorialize to abolish subordinate officials from Director of the Capital downward and add more than a hundred censors.

sentences.zh: 於是引致奸黠，共為朋黨，郡縣有不附者，陰中之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he brought in the treacherous and cunning to form factions together; commanderies and counties that did not submit were secretly struck at.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he brought in the treacherous to form factions; commanderies and counties that did not submit were secretly attacked.

sentences.zh: 于時軍國多務，凡是興師動眾，京都留守，及與諸蕃互市，皆令禦史監之。

translations.literal: At that time military and state affairs were many; whenever troops were raised, the capital was left under guard, or markets were held with the various frontier peoples—all were placed under censor supervision.
translations.idiomatic: At that time military and civil affairs were pressing; whenever troops were mobilized, the capital was left under guard, or trade was conducted with frontier peoples—censors were assigned to oversee it all.

sentences.zh: 賓客附隸，遍于郡國，侵擾百姓，帝弗之知也。

translations.literal: Clients and dependents were attached throughout commanderies and states, harassing the common people—the emperor did not know of it.
translations.idiomatic: Clients and dependents spread through every commandery, harassing the people, of which the emperor knew nothing.

sentences.zh: 以渡遼之役，進位銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Because of the Liaodong campaign he was advanced to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Silver Seal and Blue Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: For the Liaodong campaign he was promoted to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Silver Seal and Blue Ribbon.

sentences.zh: 及司馬德戡將為亂，江陽長張惠紹夜馳告之。

translations.literal: When Sima Dekan was about to rebel, the Jiangyang magistrate Zhang Huishao rode through the night to inform him.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Dekan was about to rebel, the magistrate of Jiangyang Zhang Huishao rode through the night to warn him.

sentences.zh: 蘊共惠紹謀，欲矯詔發郭下兵民，盡取榮公來護兒節度，收在外逆党宇文化及等，仍發羽林殿腳，遣范富婁等入自西苑，取梁公蕭钜及燕王處分，扣門援帝。

translations.literal: Yun together with Huishao plotted to forge an edict mobilizing troops and people outside the capital, fully take the command of Duke of Rong Laihuer, seize the outside rebel party Yuwen Huaji and others, also dispatch Forest Guard palace runners, send Fan Fulou and others in from the Western Park to take Duke of Liang Xiao Ju and the Prince of Yan for disposition, and knock on the gate to rescue the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Yun and Huishao plotted to forge an edict mobilizing capital troops and civilians, place everything under Laihuer's command, seize the rebel Yuwen Huaji and his party outside, dispatch palace guards, send Fan Fulou and others from the Western Park to secure Xiao Ju and the Prince of Yan, and storm the gate to rescue the emperor.

sentences.zh: 謀議已定，遣報虞世基。

translations.literal: When the plan was settled they sent word to Yu Shiji.
translations.idiomatic: Once the plan was set they sent word to Yu Shiji.

sentences.zh: 世基疑反者不實，抑其計。

translations.literal: Shiji doubted the rebels were real and suppressed the plan.
translations.idiomatic: Shiji doubted the report of rebellion and suppressed the plan.

sentences.zh: 須臾，難作，蘊歎曰：「謀及播郎，竟誤人事。

translations.literal: In a moment disaster struck; Yun sighed and said: "Consulting the Broadcast Gentleman—we have ruined the affair after all.
translations.idiomatic: In a moment disaster struck; Yun sighed, "Consulting that Broadcast Gentleman ruined everything.

sentences.zh: 」遂見害。

translations.literal: " He was thereupon killed.
translations.idiomatic: " He was thereupon killed.

sentences.zh: 子愔為尚輦直長，亦同日死。

translations.literal: His son Yin was Direct Attendant of the Imperial Carriage and died the same day.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yin, Direct Attendant of the Imperial Carriage, died the same day.

sentences.zh: 裴矩，字弘大，河東聞喜人也。

translations.literal: Pei Ju, style name Hongda, was a native of Wenxi in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Ju, whose style name was Hongda, came from Wenxi in Hedong.

sentences.zh: 祖他，魏都官尚書。

translations.literal: His grandfather Ta was Director of the Ministry of Justice in Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Ta was Director of the Ministry of Justice under Wei.

sentences.zh: 父訥之，齊太子舍人。

translations.literal: His father Nezhi was Crown Prince Household Attendant in Qi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Nezhi was attendant in the crown prince's household under Qi.

sentences.zh: 矩繈褓而孤，及長好學，頗愛文藻，有智數。

translations.literal: Ju was orphaned in swaddling clothes; when grown he loved learning, was quite fond of literary ornament, and had resourceful schemes.
translations.idiomatic: Ju was orphaned in infancy; when grown he loved learning, favored literary craft, and was resourceful.

sentences.zh: 世父讓之謂矩曰：「觀汝神識，足成才士，欲求宦達，當資幹世之務。

translations.literal: His uncle by senior line Rangzhi said to Ju: "Observing your spirit and insight, you are sufficient to become a talented man; if you seek official advancement, you should rely on practical affairs of the world.
translations.idiomatic: His elder uncle Rangzhi told him, "Judging your talent, you could become an accomplished man; if you seek advancement, you should master practical affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 」矩始留情世事。

translations.literal: " Ju then began to devote attention to worldly affairs.
translations.idiomatic: " Ju then turned his attention to practical affairs.

sentences.zh: 齊北平王貞為司州牧，辟為兵曹從事，轉高平王文學。

translations.literal: The Prince of Beiping Zhen of Qi was Governor of Sizhou and recruited him as Military Bureau Attendant; he was transferred to Literary Scholar for the Prince of Gaoping.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Beiping Zhen served as governor of Sizhou he recruited Ju as military bureau aide; Ju later became literary scholar to the Prince of Gaoping.

sentences.zh: 及齊亡，不得調。

translations.literal: When Qi fell he could not obtain a new appointment.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi fell he could not obtain a new appointment.

sentences.zh: 高祖為定州總管，召補記室，甚親敬之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu was Governor-General of Dingzhou he summoned him to fill the post of Recorder and was very close and respectful to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu was governor-general of Dingzhou he summoned Ju as recorder and treated him with great regard.

sentences.zh: 以母憂去職。

translations.literal: He left office on his mother's death.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 高祖作相，遣使者馳召之，參相府記室事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu became Chancellor he sent a messenger post-haste to summon him to participate in the chancellery recorder's affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu became chancellor he sent a messenger to summon Ju to serve in the chancellery secretariat.

sentences.zh: 及受禪，遷給事郎，奏舍人事。

translations.literal: When he received the abdication he was transferred to Attendant for Submitting Matters and handled palace attendant affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne Ju was made Attendant for Submitting Matters and handled palace attendant affairs.

sentences.zh: 伐陳之役，領元帥記室。

translations.literal: In the campaign against Chen he headed the commander's secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the campaign against Chen he headed the commander's secretariat.

sentences.zh: 既破丹陽，晉王廣令矩與高熲收陳圖籍。

translations.literal: After Danyang was taken, Prince of Jin Guang ordered Ju and Gao Jiong to collect Chen maps and registers.
translations.idiomatic: After Danyang fell, the Prince of Jin ordered Ju and Gao Jiong to collect Chen maps and archives.

sentences.zh: 明年，奏詔巡撫嶺南，未行而高智慧、汪文進等相聚作亂，吳、越道閉，上難遣矩行。

translations.literal: The next year he memorialized for an edict to tour and pacify Lingnan; before he set out Gao Zhihui, Wang Wenjin, and others gathered and rebelled, the Wu and Yue routes were closed, and the emperor found it hard to send Ju.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he memorialized to tour Lingnan; before he departed Gao Zhihui, Wang Wenjin, and others rebelled, the Wu and Yue routes were cut, and the emperor hesitated to send Ju.

sentences.zh: 矩請速進，上許之。

translations.literal: Ju requested to advance quickly and the emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: Ju asked to advance at once and the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 行至南康，得兵數千人。

translations.literal: When he reached Nankang he obtained several thousand troops.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching Nankang he gathered several thousand troops.

sentences.zh: 時俚帥王仲宣逼廣州，遣其所部將周師舉圍東衡州。

translations.literal: At that time the Liao chief Wang Zhongxuan pressed Guangzhou and sent his subordinate general Zhou Shiju to besiege Eastern Hengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao chief Wang Zhongxuan was pressing Guangzhou and sent his general Zhou Shiju to besiege Eastern Hengzhou.

sentences.zh: 矩與大將軍鹿願赴之，賊立九柵，屯大庾嶺，共為聲援。

translations.literal: Ju and the great general Lu Yuan went to relieve them; the rebels set up nine palisades and encamped on Dayu Ridge as mutual support.
translations.idiomatic: Ju and General Lu Yuan marched to relieve the siege; the rebels built nine palisades on Dayu Ridge to support one another.

sentences.zh: 矩進擊破之，賊懼，釋東衡州，據原長嶺。

translations.literal: Ju advanced and defeated them; the rebels feared, released Eastern Hengzhou, and held Yuan-chang Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: Ju attacked and defeated them; the rebels fled Eastern Hengzhou and held Yuan-chang Ridge.

sentences.zh: 又擊破之，遂斬師舉，進軍自南海援廣州。

translations.literal: He again defeated them, then beheaded Shiju, and advanced from Nanhai to relieve Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He defeated them again, beheaded Shiju, and marched from Nanhai to relieve Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 仲宣懼而潰散。

translations.literal: Zhongxuan feared and scattered in rout.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxuan fled and his forces scattered.

sentences.zh: 矩所綏集者二十餘州，又承制署其渠帥為刺史、縣令。

translations.literal: The more than twenty prefectures Ju pacified and gathered, he also by imperial commission appointed their chieftains as prefects and magistrates.
translations.idiomatic: Ju pacified more than twenty prefectures and, by imperial commission, appointed local chieftains as prefects and magistrates.

sentences.zh: 及還報，上大悅，命升殿勞苦之，顧謂高熲，楊素曰：「韋洸將二萬兵，不能早度嶺，朕每患其兵少。

translations.literal: When he returned to report, the emperor was greatly pleased, ordered him to ascend the hall and comfort him for his labors, and turning to Gao Jiong and Yang Su said: "Wei Guang led twenty thousand troops yet could not cross the ridge early—I always worried his force was too few.
translations.idiomatic: On his return the emperor was delighted, had him received in hall, and said to Gao Jiong and Yang Su, "Wei Guang led twenty thousand men yet could not cross the ridge in time—I always feared his force was too small.

sentences.zh: 裴矩以三千敝卒，徑至南康。

translations.literal: Pei Ju with three thousand worn troops went straight to Nankang.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Ju with three thousand worn troops went straight to Nankang.

sentences.zh: 有臣若此，朕亦何憂！

translations.literal: Having a minister like this, what have I to worry about!
translations.idiomatic: With a minister like this, what have I to fear!

sentences.zh: 」以功拜開府，賜爵聞喜縣公，賚物二千段。

translations.literal: " For his merit he was appointed Opening the Government, granted the title Duke of Wenxi County, and given two thousand bales of goods.
translations.idiomatic: " For his merit he was made Opening the Government, ennobled as Duke of Wenxi County, and given two thousand bales of gifts.

sentences.zh: 除民部侍郎，尋遷內史侍郎。

translations.literal: He was appointed Vice Director of the Ministry of Population and soon transferred to Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Vice Director of the Ministry of Population and soon promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 臣聞禹定九州，導河不逾積石；

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that Yu fixed the nine provinces and channeled the river no farther than Jishi;
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that Yu fixed the nine provinces and channeled the Yellow River no farther than Jishi;

sentences.zh: 秦兼六國，設防止及臨洮。

translations.literal: Qin united the six states and set defenses only as far as Lintao.
translations.idiomatic: Qin united the six states and set its frontier defenses only as far as Lintao.

sentences.zh: 故知西胡雜種，僻居遐裔，禮教之所不及，書典之所罕傳。

translations.literal: Thus one knows the mixed tribes of the western Hu dwell far in remote borderlands, where ritual teaching does not reach and written canons are rarely transmitted.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the mixed tribes of the western Hu live in remote borderlands beyond ritual teaching and rarely recorded in our classics.

sentences.zh: 自漢氏興基，開拓河右，始稱名號者，有三十六國，其後分立，乃五十五王。

translations.literal: From the Han dynasty's rise and foundation, opening the lands west of the river, those first bearing titles numbered thirty-six states; later they split apart into fifty-five kings.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Han rose and opened the lands west of the river, thirty-six states first bore titles; later they split into fifty-five kingdoms.

sentences.zh: 仍置校尉、都護，以存招撫。

translations.literal: They still established colonels and protectors to preserve recruitment and pacification.
translations.idiomatic: They still appointed colonels and protectors to win submission and keep peace.

sentences.zh: 然叛服不恆，屢經征戰，後漢之世，頻廢此官。

translations.literal: Yet rebellion and submission were inconstant and campaigns were frequent; in the Later Han era this office was often abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Yet rebellion and submission shifted constantly and campaigns were frequent; under Later Han this office was often abolished.

sentences.zh: 雖大宛以來，略知戶數，而諸國山川，未有名目。

translations.literal: Though since Dayuan one roughly knew household counts, the mountains and rivers of the various states had no established names.
translations.idiomatic: Though since Dayuan household counts were roughly known, the mountains and rivers of the various states had no established names.

sentences.zh: 至如姓氏風土，服章物產，全無纂錄，世所弗聞。

translations.literal: As for surnames, local customs, dress, products, and goods, there was wholly no compilation—the world had not heard of them.
translations.idiomatic: Surnames, local customs, dress, and products were wholly unrecorded and unknown to the world.

sentences.zh: 複以春秋遞謝，年代久遠，兼併誅討，互有興亡。
