translations.literal: Moreover, as springs and autumns succeeded one another and ages grew remote, annexation and punitive campaigns alternated and rise and fall replaced one another.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, as ages passed, annexation and punitive campaigns alternated and states rose and fell in turn.

sentences.zh: 或地是故邦，改從今號，或人非舊類，因襲昔名。

translations.literal: Some lands were old states but changed to present titles; some people were not of the old kind yet inherited former names.
translations.idiomatic: Some lands were old states under new names; some peoples were not the old tribes yet kept former titles.

sentences.zh: 兼複部民交錯，封疆移改，戎狄音殊，事難窮驗。

translations.literal: Moreover clans and peoples intermingled, borders shifted, Rong and Di languages differed—affairs were hard to verify exhaustively.
translations.idiomatic: Clans intermingled, borders shifted, and frontier languages differed—facts were hard to verify.

sentences.zh: 於闐之北，蔥嶺以東，考于前史，三十余國。

translations.literal: North of Khotan and east of the Onion Mountains, examining earlier histories, there were more than thirty states.
translations.idiomatic: North of Khotan and east of the Onion Mountains, earlier histories record more than thirty states.

sentences.zh: 其後更相屠滅，僅有十存。

translations.literal: Afterward they slaughtered and destroyed one another; only about ten survived.
translations.idiomatic: Later they slaughtered one another until only about ten survived.

sentences.zh: 自餘淪沒，掃地俱盡，空有丘墟，不可記識。

translations.literal: The rest sank away and were swept clean away; only mounds and ruins remained, beyond recording and recognition.
translations.idiomatic: The rest perished utterly, leaving only ruins beyond identification.

sentences.zh: 皇上膺天育物，無隔華夷，率土黔黎，莫不慕化。

translations.literal: Your Majesty receives Heaven and nurtures things, without barrier between Hua and Yi; all the black-haired people within the realm none do not admire transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty receives Heaven's mandate and nurtures all beings without distinction between Chinese and barbarian; all the people within the realm admire your civilizing influence.

sentences.zh: 風行所及，日入以來，職貢皆通，無遠不至。

translations.literal: Where the wind of influence reaches, from the sun's setting onward, tribute duties all connect—none so far they do not arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Where your influence reaches, even to the land of the setting sun, tribute routes are open and none are too distant to come.

sentences.zh: 臣既因撫納，監知關市，尋討書傳，訪采胡人，或有所疑，即詳眾口。

translations.literal: Your servant, having through pacification and reception overseen the frontier markets, searched books and transmissions and interviewed Hu people; when there was doubt he at once examined the many mouths.
translations.idiomatic: Through pacification and reception I oversaw the frontier markets, searched written sources, and interviewed foreigners; whenever in doubt I cross-checked with many informants.

sentences.zh: 依其本國服飾儀形，王及庶人，各顯容止，即丹青模寫，為《西域圖記》，共成三卷，合四十四國。

translations.literal: According to each state's native dress, ornaments, and forms, king and commoner each displaying bearing and manner, I then painted and copied them, making "Records of the Western Regions with Maps," three scrolls in all, comprising forty-four states.
translations.idiomatic: According to each state's dress and customs I depicted kings and commoners alike in paint, producing Records of the Western Regions with Maps in three scrolls covering forty-four states.

sentences.zh: 仍別造地圖，窮其要害。

translations.literal: I also separately made maps exhaustively showing their strategic points.
translations.idiomatic: I also made separate maps showing their strategic points in full.

sentences.zh: 從西頃以去，北海之南，縱橫所亙，將二萬里。

translations.literal: From west of Xiqing south of the Northern Sea, the area spanned length and breadth is nearly twenty thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: From west of Xiqing to south of the Northern Sea, the region spans nearly twenty thousand li.

sentences.zh: 諒由富商大賈，周遊經涉，故諸國之事，罔不遍知。

translations.literal: Surely because great merchants and traders toured and passed through, affairs of the various states are without exception broadly known.
translations.idiomatic: Surely because great merchants traveled these routes, affairs of the various states are widely known.

sentences.zh: 複有幽荒遠地，卒訪難曉，不可憑虛，是以致闕。

translations.literal: There are also remote lands in shadowed wilderness where sudden inquiry is hard to understand; one cannot rely on the empty, and therefore omissions are made.
translations.idiomatic: Some remote wilderness areas cannot be verified and are therefore omitted rather than invented.

sentences.zh: 而二漢相踵，西域為傳，戶民數十，即稱國王，徒有名號，乃乖其實。

translations.literal: Yet the two Han dynasties followed in succession; in the Western Regions tradition, a few dozen households and people at once were called kings—mere titles empty of reality.
translations.idiomatic: Under the two Han dynasties, states of only a few dozen households were called kingdoms in the Western Regions records—titles empty of reality.

sentences.zh: 今者所編，皆餘千戶，利盡西海，多產珍異。

translations.literal: Those compiled now all have more than a thousand households, profit reaching the western sea, producing many rare and exotic goods.
translations.idiomatic: Those I record now all have more than a thousand households, trade reaching the western sea, and produce many rare goods.

sentences.zh: 其山居之屬，非有國名，及部落小者，多亦不載。

translations.literal: Mountain-dwelling groups without state names and small tribes are mostly also not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Mountain peoples without state names and small tribes are mostly omitted.

sentences.zh: 發自敦煌，至於西海，凡為三道，各有襟帶。

translations.literal: Starting from Dunhuang to the western sea, there are in all three routes, each with its connecting belt of states.
translations.idiomatic: From Dunhuang to the western sea there are three routes, each with its chain of states.

sentences.zh: 北道從伊吾，經蒲類海鐵勒部突厥可汗庭，度北流河水，至拂菻國，達於西海。

translations.literal: The northern route goes from Yiwu, passes the Pulei Sea, the Tiele tribes, and the Turk qaghan's court, crosses the north-flowing river, reaches Fulin state, and arrives at the western sea.
translations.idiomatic: The northern route runs from Yiwu past the Pulei Sea, the Tiele tribes, and the Turk qaghan's court, crosses the north-flowing river, reaches Fulin, and arrives at the western sea.

sentences.zh: 其中道從高昌、焉耆、龜茲、疏勒、度蔥嶺，又經鈸汗、蘇對沙那國、康國、曹國、何國、大小安國、穆國，至波斯，達於西海。

translations.literal: The central route goes from Gaochang, Yanqi, Kucha, Shule, crosses the Onion Mountains, then passes Bohhan, Suduoshana, Kang, Cao, He, Greater and Lesser An, Mu, to Persia and the western sea.
translations.idiomatic: The central route runs from Gaochang, Yanqi, Kucha, and Shule across the Onion Mountains, then through Bohhan, Suduoshana, Kang, Cao, He, Greater and Lesser An, and Mu to Persia and the western sea.

sentences.zh: 其南道從鄯善，於闐，硃俱波、喝槃陀，度蔥嶺，又經護密、吐火羅、挹怛、忛延，漕國，至北婆羅門，達於西海。

translations.literal: The southern route goes from Shanshan, Khotan, Zhujubo, Hepantuo, crosses the Onion Mountains, then passes Humi, Tuhuoluo, Yidan, Qianyan, Caoguo, to North Brahmana and the western sea.
translations.idiomatic: The southern route runs from Shanshan, Khotan, Zhujubo, and Hepantuo across the Onion Mountains, then through Humi, Tuhuoluo, Yidan, Qianyan, and Caoguo to North India and the western sea.

sentences.zh: 其三道諸國，亦各自有路，南北交通。

translations.literal: The states of these three routes also each have their own paths connecting north and south.
translations.idiomatic: The states along these three routes also have their own paths linking north and south.

sentences.zh: 其東女國、南婆羅門國等，並隨其所往，諸處得達。

translations.literal: The Eastern Women's State, Southern Brahmana state, and others can all be reached according to where one goes.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Women's State, Southern India, and others can all be reached by the appropriate route.

sentences.zh: 故知伊吾、高昌、鄯善，並西域之門戶也。

translations.literal: Thus one knows Yiwu, Gaochang, and Shanshan are all gateways of the Western Regions.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Yiwu, Gaochang, and Shanshan are the gateways to the Western Regions.

sentences.zh: 總湊敦煌，是其咽喉之地。

translations.literal: All converge on Dunhuang—this is the throat and gullet place.
translations.idiomatic: All converge on Dunhuang, its strategic throat.

sentences.zh: 以國家威德，將士驍雄，泛濛汜而揚旌，越昆侖而躍馬，易如反掌，何往不至！

translations.literal: With the state's majesty and virtue, officers and soldiers fierce and heroic, sailing Mengsi and raising banners, crossing Kunlun and leaping horses—it is easy as turning the palm; where would one not arrive!
translations.idiomatic: With the state's majesty and our fierce soldiers, to sail distant waters and cross Kunlun is as easy as turning the hand—where could we not go!

sentences.zh: 但突厥、吐渾分領羌胡之國，為其擁遏，故朝貢不通。

translations.literal: Only the Turks and Tuyuhun divided rule over the Qiang and Hu states and blocked them, so court tribute did not pass through.
translations.idiomatic: Only the Turks and Tuyuhun, controlling the Qiang and Hu states, blocked the routes so tribute could not pass.

sentences.zh: 今並因商人密送誠款，引領翹首，願為臣妾。

translations.literal: Now all through merchants secretly sending sincere pledges, they lead and crane their necks, wishing to become subjects and concubines.
translations.idiomatic: Now through merchants they secretly send pledges of loyalty, eager to submit and become your subjects.

sentences.zh: 聖情含養，澤及普天，服而撫之，務存安輯。

translations.literal: Sacred feeling embraces and nurtures, favor reaching all under Heaven; submit them and comfort them, striving to preserve peace and order.
translations.idiomatic: Your sacred grace embraces all under Heaven; receive them and comfort them, striving for peace and order.

sentences.zh: 故皇華遣使，弗動兵車，諸蕃即從，渾、厥可滅。

translations.literal: Therefore the imperial envoy is sent without moving chariots of war; the various frontier peoples will at once follow, and Tuyuhun and the Turks can be destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore send the imperial envoy without moving armies; the frontier peoples will follow, and Tuyuhun and the Turks can be destroyed.

sentences.zh: 混一戎夏，其在茲乎！

translations.literal: Uniting Rong and Xia—is it not here!
translations.idiomatic: Uniting Chinese and barbarian—is the moment not now!

sentences.zh: 不有所記，無以表威化之遠也。

translations.literal: Without some record, there is no means to display how far majestic transformation reaches.
translations.idiomatic: Without recording these matters, there is no way to show how far your civilizing power reaches.

sentences.zh: 帝大悅，賜物五百段，每日引矩至禦坐，親問西方之事。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and bestowed five hundred bales of goods; daily he brought Ju to the imperial seat and personally asked about western affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted and gave five hundred bales of gifts; daily he summoned Ju to the imperial seat to ask about the west.

sentences.zh: 矩盛言胡中多諸寶物，吐谷渾易可併吞。

translations.literal: Ju strongly said that among the Hu were many treasures and goods and that Tuyuhun could easily be swallowed whole.
translations.idiomatic: Ju stressed that the frontier lands held many treasures and that Tuyuhun could easily be conquered.

sentences.zh: 帝由是甘心，將通西域，四夷經略，鹹以委之。

translations.literal: The emperor thereby set his heart on it, intending to open the Western Regions; strategy toward the four Yi was all entrusted to him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was persuaded and intended to open the Western Regions; strategy toward the four frontiers was all entrusted to him.

sentences.zh: 轉民部侍郎，未視事，遷黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Ministry of Population; before taking office he was moved to Yellow Gate Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Ministry of Population but before taking office was promoted to Yellow Gate Attendant.

sentences.zh: 帝複令矩往張掖，引致西蕃，至者十余國。

translations.literal: The emperor again ordered Ju to Zhangye to bring in the western frontier peoples; more than ten states arrived.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again sent Ju to Zhangye to bring in western peoples; more than ten states came.

sentences.zh: 大業三年，帝有事于恆嶽，鹹來助祭。

translations.literal: In the third year of Daye the emperor performed rites at Mount Heng; all came to assist in the sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Daye the emperor performed rites at Mount Heng; all came to assist at the sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 帝將巡河右，複令矩往敦煌。

translations.literal: When the emperor was about to tour the west of the river he again ordered Ju to Dunhuang.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor was about to tour the Hexi region he again sent Ju to Dunhuang.

sentences.zh: 矩遣使說高昌王麹伯雅及伊吾吐屯設等，啖以厚利，導使入朝。

translations.literal: Ju sent envoys to persuade the King of Gaochang Qu Boya and the Yiwu Tutan she and others, baiting them with rich profit and guiding them to come to court.
translations.idiomatic: Ju sent envoys to persuade the King of Gaochang Qu Boya, the Yiwu chieftain, and others with rich rewards, guiding them to court.

sentences.zh: 及帝西巡，次燕支山，高昌王、伊吾設等及西蕃胡二十七國，謁于道左。

translations.literal: When the emperor toured west and halted at Mount Yanzhi, the King of Gaochang, the Yiwu she, and twenty-seven western Hu states paid homage on the left of the road.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor toured west and halted at Mount Yanzhi, the King of Gaochang, the Yiwu chieftain, and twenty-seven western states paid homage along the route.

sentences.zh: 皆令佩金玉，被錦罽，焚香奏樂，歌儛喧噪。

translations.literal: All were ordered to wear jade and gold, be clothed in brocade and felt, burn incense and perform music, singing and dancing in noisy clamor.
translations.idiomatic: All were dressed in jade, gold, and brocade, burned incense, played music, and sang and danced in noisy celebration.

sentences.zh: 複令武威、張掖士女盛飾縱觀，騎乘填咽，周亙數十裡，以示中國之盛。

translations.literal: He again ordered the men and women of Wuwei and Zhangye to adorn themselves lavishly and watch freely; riders and carriages packed the road for several tens of li, to show the splendor of China.
translations.idiomatic: He also had the people of Wuwei and Zhangye dress in splendor to watch; riders and carriages packed the roads for miles, displaying China's grandeur.

sentences.zh: 帝見而大悅。

translations.literal: The emperor saw it and was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor saw this and was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 竟破吐谷渾，拓地數千里，並遣兵戍之。

translations.literal: In the end they broke Tuyuhun, extended territory several thousand li, and also sent troops to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: They finally defeated Tuyuhun, extended territory by thousands of li, and garrisoned troops there.

sentences.zh: 每歲委輸巨億萬計，諸蕃懾懼，朝貢相續。

translations.literal: Each year tribute deliveries amounted to hundreds of millions; the various frontier peoples were in awe and fear, and court tribute followed in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Each year tribute worth hundreds of millions arrived; the frontier peoples were awed and sent tribute in succession.

sentences.zh: 帝謂矩有綏懷之略，進位銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: The emperor said Ju had a strategy of pacification and reassurance and advanced him to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Silver Seal and Blue Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said Ju had a gift for winning over the frontier and promoted him to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Silver Seal and Blue Ribbon.

sentences.zh: 其冬，帝至東都，矩以蠻夷朝貢者多，諷帝令都下大戲。

translations.literal: That winter the emperor reached the eastern capital; Ju, because many barbarians and Yi came to pay tribute, indirectly urged the emperor to hold great entertainments in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the emperor reached the eastern capital; as many foreigners came to pay tribute, Ju urged the emperor to hold grand festivities in the capital.

sentences.zh: 征四方奇技異藝，陳於端門街，衣錦綺、珥金翠者以十數萬。

translations.literal: He summoned rare skills and exotic arts from the four directions and displayed them on Duangmen Street; those wearing brocade and silk and dangling gold and kingfisher feathers numbered in the hundreds of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Rare skills and exotic arts from every quarter were displayed on Duangmen Street; hundreds of thousands wore brocade and gold ornaments.

sentences.zh: 又勒百官及民士女列坐棚閣而縱觀焉。

translations.literal: He also ordered the hundred officials and common men and women to sit in rows on pavilion galleries and watch freely.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered officials and commoners alike to sit in pavilion galleries and watch.

sentences.zh: 皆被服鮮麗，終月乃罷。

translations.literal: All were clothed in fresh splendor; only after a full month did it end.
translations.idiomatic: All were dressed in splendor; the spectacle lasted a full month.

sentences.zh: 又令三市店肆皆設帷帳，盛列酒食，遣掌蕃率蠻夷與民貿易，所至之處，悉令邀延就坐，醉飽而散。

translations.literal: He also ordered the shops of the three markets to set up canopies and lavishly array food and drink, sending frontier commissioners to lead barbarians and Yi to trade with the people; wherever they went all were invited to sit, and they dispersed drunk and full.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered market shops to set up canopies with food and drink, had frontier commissioners lead foreigners to trade with locals, and had them invited to feast wherever they went until drunk and sated.

sentences.zh: 蠻夷嗟歎，謂中國為神仙。

translations.literal: The barbarians and Yi sighed in admiration and called China the realm of immortals.
translations.idiomatic: The foreigners sighed in wonder and called China a land of immortals.

sentences.zh: 帝稱其至誠，顧謂宇文述、牛弘曰：「裴矩大識朕意，凡所陳奏，皆朕之成算。

translations.literal: The emperor praised his utmost sincerity and turning to Yuwen Shu and Niu Hong said: "Pei Ju greatly understands my intent; whatever he memorializes is all my completed plan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised his sincerity and said to Yuwen Shu and Niu Hong, "Pei Ju understands my mind; whatever he submits is already my settled plan.

sentences.zh: 未發之頃，矩輒以聞。

translations.literal: Before it is issued, Ju has already reported it.
translations.idiomatic: Before I even announce it, Ju has already reported it.

sentences.zh: 自非奉國用心，孰能若是！

translations.literal: If not for devotion to the state in heart, who could be like this!
translations.idiomatic: Without true devotion to the state, who could do this!

sentences.zh: 」帝遣將軍薛世雄城伊吾，令矩共往經略。

translations.literal: " The emperor sent General Xue Shixiong to fortify Yiwu and ordered Ju to go together to plan strategy.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor sent General Xue Shixiong to fortify Yiwu and ordered Ju to join him in planning.

sentences.zh: 矩諷諭西域諸國曰：「天子為蕃人交易懸遠，所以城伊吾耳。

translations.literal: Ju indirectly instructed the states of the Western Regions, saying: "The Son of Heaven, because frontier people's trade is far and suspended, therefore fortifies Yiwu—that is all.
translations.idiomatic: Ju explained to the Western Regions states, "The emperor fortifies Yiwu only because frontier trade routes are long and difficult.

sentences.zh: 」鹹以為然，不復來競。

translations.literal: " All thought it so and no longer came to compete.
translations.idiomatic: " All agreed and ceased their objections.

sentences.zh: 及還，賜錢四十萬。

translations.literal: When he returned he was bestowed four hundred thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was given four hundred thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 矩又白狀，令反間射匱，潛攻處羅，語在《突厥傳》。

translations.literal: Ju again reported in a memorial, ordering counter-intelligence against Shekui and a secret attack on Chuluo—the account is in "Biography of the Turks."
translations.idiomatic: Ju again memorialized, setting counter-intelligence against Shekui and a secret attack on Chuluo, as told in the Biography of the Turks.

sentences.zh: 後處羅為射匱所迫，竟隨使者入朝。

translations.literal: Later Chuluo, pressed by Shekui, in the end followed envoys to court.
translations.idiomatic: Later Chuluo, pressed by Shekui, finally came to court with the envoys.

sentences.zh: 帝大悅，賜矩以貂裘及西域珍器。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and bestowed on Ju sable fur coats and rare objects from the Western Regions.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted and gave Ju sable coats and rare treasures from the west.

sentences.zh: 從帝巡於塞北，幸啟民帳。

translations.literal: He followed the emperor touring the northern frontier and visited Qimin's tent.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied the emperor on a tour of the northern frontier and visited Qimin's tent.

sentences.zh: 時高麗遣使先通於突厥，啟民不敢隱，引之見帝。

translations.literal: At that time Goguryeo sent envoys first to communicate with the Turks; Qimin did not dare conceal it and led them to see the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Goguryeo had sent envoys to the Turks first; Qimin did not dare conceal it and presented them to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 矩因奏狀曰：「高麗之地，本孤竹國也。

translations.literal: Ju thereupon memorialized, saying: "The land of Goguryeo was originally the state of Guzhu.
translations.idiomatic: Ju memorialized, "The land of Goguryeo was originally the state of Guzhu.

sentences.zh: 周代以之封於箕子，漢世分為三郡，晉氏亦統遼東。

translations.literal: The Zhou dynasty enfeoffed Jizi with it; the Han era divided it into three commanderies; the Jin house also ruled Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou enfeoffed Jizi there; Han divided it into three commanderies; Jin also ruled Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 今乃不臣，別為外域，故先帝疾焉，欲征之久矣。

translations.literal: Now they do not submit and stand apart as an outer realm; therefore the former emperor was vexed and wished to campaign against them long ago.
translations.idiomatic: Now they refuse submission and stand apart as a foreign realm; the former emperor long wished to campaign against them.

sentences.zh: 但以楊諒不肖，師出無功。

translations.literal: But because Yang Liang was unworthy, the army went forth without achievement.
translations.idiomatic: But because Yang Liang proved unworthy, the campaign achieved nothing.

sentences.zh: 當陛下之時，安得不事，使此冠帶之境，仍為蠻貊之鄉乎？

translations.literal: In Your Majesty's time, how can we not serve, allowing this realm of caps and belts to remain a land of barbarians and Mo?
translations.idiomatic: In Your Majesty's time, how can we tolerate this civilized land remaining barbarian territory?

sentences.zh: 今其使者朝于突厥，親見啟民，合國從化，必懼皇靈之遠暢，慮後伏之先亡。

translations.literal: Now their envoys attend court among the Turks and personally see Qimin; the whole state follows transformation—they must fear the far reach of imperial numen and worry that later submission will perish first.
translations.idiomatic: Now their envoys have seen Qimin at the Turks' court; seeing the whole realm submit, they must fear imperial power and worry they will be destroyed if they delay.

sentences.zh: 脅令入朝，當可致也。

translations.literal: Coerce them to come to court and it can be achieved.
translations.idiomatic: Pressure them to come to court and they can be brought in.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「如何？

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "How?
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor asked, "How?

sentences.zh: 」矩曰：「請面詔其使，放還本國，遣語其王，令速朝觀。

translations.literal: " Ju said: "Please face-to-face instruct their envoy, release him to return to his state, and send word to their king ordering him to come quickly to court audience.
translations.idiomatic: " Ju said, "Face their envoy, send him home, and tell their king to come to court at once.

sentences.zh: 不然者，當率突厥，即日誅之。

translations.literal: If not, lead the Turks and execute them that very day.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise lead the Turks and destroy them immediately.

sentences.zh: 」帝納焉。

translations.literal: " The emperor adopted it.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 高元不用命，始建征遼之策。

translations.literal: Gao Yuan did not obey orders; the strategy to campaign against Liaodong was first established.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yuan disobeyed; the Liaodong campaign was then planned.

sentences.zh: 王師臨遼，以本官領武賁郎將。

translations.literal: When the royal army reached Liaodong he held his original office and led Martial Guard Cavalry Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial army reached Liaodong he served as Martial Guard Cavalry Commandant.

sentences.zh: 明年，複從至遼東。

translations.literal: The next year he again followed to Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he again accompanied the campaign to Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 兵部侍郎斛斯政亡入高麗，帝令矩兼掌兵事。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Ministry of War Husizheng fled into Goguryeo; the emperor ordered Ju concurrently to manage military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director of War Husizheng fled to Goguryeo; the emperor had Ju also manage military affairs.

sentences.zh: 以前後渡遼之役，進位右光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Because of the successive Liaodong crossing campaigns he was advanced to Right Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: For the Liaodong campaigns he was promoted to Right Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 于時皇綱不振，人皆變節，左翊衛大將軍宇文述、內史侍郎虞世基等用事，文武多以賄聞。

translations.literal: At that time the imperial net was slack and people all changed their loyalty; Left Guard General Yuwen Shu, Secretariat Vice Director Yu Shiji, and others held power, and civil and military officials were mostly known for bribes.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial order was failing and men changed loyalty; Yuwen Shu, Yu Shiji, and others held power, and officials were widely known for taking bribes.

sentences.zh: 唯矩守常，無贓穢之響，以是為世所稱。

translations.literal: Only Ju kept to constancy without a reputation for corrupt filth, and therefore was praised by the world.
translations.idiomatic: Only Ju remained upright without a reputation for corruption, and for this was praised.

sentences.zh: 還至涿郡，帝以楊玄感初平，令矩安集隴右。

translations.literal: Returning to Zhuo Commandery, because Yang Xuangan had just been pacified, the emperor ordered Ju to settle and pacify Longyou.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned to Zhuo Commandery, the emperor—Yang Xuangan's rebellion having just been crushed—sent Ju to restore order in Longyou.

sentences.zh: 因之會寧，存問曷沙那部落，遣闕達度設寇吐谷渾，頻有虜獲，部落致富。

translations.literal: Taking advantage of this he met at Huining, inquired after the Ashina tribe, and sent Quedu She to raid Tuyuhun; there were frequent captures of booty and the tribe grew wealthy.
translations.idiomatic: From there he went to Huining to inquire after the Ashina tribe and sent Quedu She against Tuyuhun; repeated raids brought rich spoils and made the tribe prosperous.

sentences.zh: 還而奏狀，帝大賞之。

translations.literal: On returning he submitted a report; the emperor greatly rewarded him.
translations.idiomatic: He reported on his return, and the emperor richly rewarded him.

sentences.zh: 後從師至懷遠鎮，詔護北蕃軍事。

translations.literal: Later he followed the army to Huaiyuan Fort; an edict appointed him to oversee northern frontier military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Later he marched with the army to Huaiyuan Fort, where an edict put him in charge of northern frontier military affairs.

sentences.zh: 矩以始畢可汗部眾漸盛，獻策分其勢，將以宗女嫁其弟叱吉設，拜為南面可汗。

translations.literal: Ju, because Shibi Khan's following was gradually growing strong, submitted a plan to divide his power: he would marry an imperial clanswoman to Shibi's younger brother Chiji She and enfeoff him as Southern Khan.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Shibi Khan's following grow ever stronger, Ju proposed splitting his power: marry an imperial clanswoman to Shibi's brother Chiji She and install him as Southern Khan.

sentences.zh: 叱吉不敢受，始畢聞而漸怨。

translations.literal: Chiji did not dare accept; Shibi heard of it and gradually grew resentful.
translations.idiomatic: Chiji dared not accept; when Shibi learned of the plan, resentment took root.

sentences.zh: 矩又言於帝曰：「突厥本淳，易可離間，但由其內多有群胡，盡皆桀黠，教導之耳。

translations.literal: Ju again said to the emperor: "The Turks are by nature simple and can easily be divided—but within them are many bands of Hu, all fierce and cunning; it is they who teach and guide them.
translations.idiomatic: Ju told the emperor again, "The Turks are simple by nature and easily set against one another—but many Hu bands among them are fierce and cunning; they are the ones who truly steer them."

sentences.zh: 臣聞史蜀胡悉尤多奸計，幸于始畢，請誘殺之。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that Shishu Husi in particular has many treacherous schemes and enjoys Shibi's favor. I request that we lure and kill him.
translations.idiomatic: "I have heard that Shishu Husi is especially full of treacherous schemes and stands high in Shibi's favor. I ask leave to lure him out and kill him."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「善。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "Good.
translations.idiomatic: " "Good," said the emperor.

sentences.zh: 」矩因遣人告胡悉曰：「天子大出珍物，今在馬邑，欲共蕃內多作交關。

translations.literal: " Ju then sent someone to tell Husi: "The Son of Heaven has brought out many rare treasures; they are now at Mayi. He wishes to conduct much trade with the frontier peoples within the borders.
translations.idiomatic: " Ju then sent word to Husi: "The Son of Heaven has brought out great stores of rare goods at Mayi and wishes to trade freely with the frontier peoples."

sentences.zh: 若前來者，即得好物。

translations.literal: Those who come first will obtain fine goods.
translations.idiomatic: "Whoever arrives first will get the best of them."

sentences.zh: 」胡悉貪而信之，不告始畢，率其部落，盡驅六畜，星馳爭進，冀先互市。

translations.literal: " Husi, greedy, believed it; without informing Shibi he led his tribe, drove all their livestock, and raced forward like stars, hoping to trade first.
translations.idiomatic: " Greedy and credulous, Husi told Shibi nothing. He led his whole tribe, drove off every head of livestock, and galloped night and day to reach the market first.

sentences.zh: 矩伏兵馬邑下，誘而斬之。

translations.literal: Ju lay in ambush below Mayi, lured him in, and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Ju hid troops below Mayi, drew him in, and cut off his head.

sentences.zh: 詔報始畢曰：「史蜀胡悉忽領部落走來至此，雲背可汗，請我容納。

translations.literal: An edict reported to Shibi: "Shishu Husi suddenly led his tribe in flight here, saying he had turned against the khan and asking us to receive him.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was sent to Shibi: "Shishu Husi has suddenly fled here at the head of his tribe, claiming he has turned against you and begging us to shelter him."

sentences.zh: 突厥既是我臣，彼有背叛，我當共殺。

translations.literal: Since the Turks are already our subjects, when one of them betrays, we ought to kill him together.
translations.idiomatic: "The Turks are our subjects; when one betrays, we should kill him together."

sentences.zh: 今已斬之，故令往報。

translations.literal: He has now been executed; we therefore send this report.
translations.idiomatic: "He has already been executed, and we send word accordingly."

sentences.zh: 」始畢亦知其狀，由是不朝。

translations.literal: " Shibi also knew the truth of the matter and for this reason ceased coming to court.
translations.idiomatic: " Shibi knew what had really happened and from then on stopped coming to court.

sentences.zh: 十一年，帝北巡狩，始畢率騎數十萬，圍帝於雁門。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year the emperor toured north on hunt; Shibi led several hundred thousand horsemen and besieged the emperor at Yanmen.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year the emperor went north on tour; Shibi led several hundred thousand horsemen and trapped him at Yanmen.

sentences.zh: 詔令矩與虞世基每宿朝堂，以待顧問。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Ju and Yu Shiji to sleep each night in the audience hall, waiting to be consulted.
translations.idiomatic: An edict had Ju and Yu Shiji sleep in the audience hall every night, ready to be summoned for counsel.

sentences.zh: 及圍解，從至東都。

translations.literal: When the siege was lifted, he followed to the eastern capital.
translations.idiomatic: When the siege was broken, he followed the emperor to the eastern capital.

sentences.zh: 屬射匱可汗遣其猶子，率西蕃諸胡朝貢，詔矩宴接之。

translations.literal: At this time Shekui Khan sent his nephew leading the various Hu of the western frontier to pay tribute; an edict ordered Ju to feast and receive them.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Shekui Khan sent his nephew at the head of the western frontier peoples to pay tribute, and Ju was ordered to feast and receive them.

sentences.zh: 尋從幸江都宮。

translations.literal: Soon after he followed in the imperial retinue to the Jiangdu Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he accompanied the emperor to the Jiangdu Palace.

sentences.zh: 時四方盜賊蜂起，郡縣上奏者不可勝計。

translations.literal: At that time bandits and rebels swarmed from the four directions; the memorials from commands and counties were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels were rising everywhere; reports from commands and counties poured in beyond count.

sentences.zh: 矩言之，帝怒，遣矩詣京師接候蕃客，以疾不行。

translations.literal: When Ju spoke of it, the emperor grew angry and sent Ju to the capital to receive and attend frontier guests; Ju did not go, pleading illness.
translations.idiomatic: When Ju raised the matter, the emperor flew into a rage and ordered him to the capital to receive foreign envoys; Ju pleaded illness and did not go.

sentences.zh: 及義兵入關，帝令虞世基就宅問矩方略。

translations.literal: When the righteous armies entered the passes, the emperor had Yu Shiji go to Ju's residence to ask his strategy.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebel armies entered the passes, the emperor sent Yu Shiji to Ju's home to ask his counsel.

sentences.zh: 矩曰：「太原有變，京畿不靜，遙為處分，恐失事機。

translations.literal: Ju said: "There is trouble at Taiyuan and the capital region is unsettled; to manage affairs from afar, I fear we will miss the moment.
translations.idiomatic: Ju said, "Taiyuan is in turmoil and the capital region is unsettled; if we try to manage things from a distance, I fear we will lose our chance."

sentences.zh: 唯願鑾輿早還，方可平定。

translations.literal: I only wish the imperial carriage would return soon—only then can things be settled.
translations.idiomatic: "I only pray the imperial carriage returns at once—only then can order be restored."

sentences.zh: 」矩複起視事。

translations.literal: " Ju then rose again to attend to affairs.
translations.idiomatic: " Ju then returned to duty.

sentences.zh: 俄而驍衛大將軍屈突通敗問至，矩以聞，帝失色。

translations.literal: Before long word arrived that General of the Valiant Guard Qu Tu Tong had been defeated; Ju reported it and the emperor's face changed color.
translations.idiomatic: Before long came word that Qu Tu Tong, General of the Valiant Guard, had been defeated; Ju reported it, and the emperor went pale.

sentences.zh: 矩素勤謹，未嘗忤物，又見天下方亂，恐為身禍，其待遇人，多過其所望，故雖至廝役，皆得其歡心。

translations.literal: Ju had always been diligent and careful and never gave offense; now seeing the empire in turmoil, he feared personal disaster, and in his treatment of others he often exceeded what they hoped for—so even down to servants all won his goodwill.
translations.idiomatic: Ju had always been diligent and careful, never giving offense; now, with the realm in chaos and fearing for his own safety, he treated everyone better than they expected—even servants came to love him.

sentences.zh: 時從駕驍果數有逃散，帝憂之，以問矩。

translations.literal: At that time the Valiant Corps in the imperial retinue repeatedly deserted; the emperor worried and asked Ju.
translations.idiomatic: The Valiant Corps in the imperial train were deserting in numbers; the emperor was troubled and asked Ju what to do.

sentences.zh: 矩答曰：「方今車駕留此，已經二年。

translations.literal: Ju replied: "At present the imperial carriage has remained here already two years.
translations.idiomatic: Ju answered, "The imperial carriage has now stayed here two full years.

sentences.zh: 驍果之徒，盡無家口，人無匹合，則不能久安。

translations.literal: The Valiant Corps have no families at all; without spouses, men cannot long remain settled.
translations.idiomatic: The Valiant Corps have no wives or children; without families, men cannot stay content for long."

sentences.zh: 臣請聽兵士于此納室。

translations.literal: Your subject requests permission for the soldiers to take wives here.
translations.idiomatic: "I ask that the soldiers be allowed to take wives here."

sentences.zh: 」帝大喜曰：「公定多智，此奇計也。

translations.literal: " The emperor was greatly pleased and said: "You must be very wise—this is a marvelous plan!
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor was delighted. "You are full of wisdom—what a brilliant scheme!"

sentences.zh: 」因令矩檢校，為將士等娶妻。

translations.literal: " He then ordered Ju to oversee the matter and find wives for the officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: " He put Ju in charge of finding wives for the officers and men.

sentences.zh: 矩召江都境內寡婦及未嫁女，皆集宮監，又召將帥及兵等恣其所取。

translations.literal: Ju summoned widows and unmarried daughters within the Jiangdu region, all gathered under palace supervision, and summoned commanders and soldiers to take whom they wished.
translations.idiomatic: Ju gathered every widow and unmarried woman in the Jiangdu region under palace supervision, then let commanders and soldiers choose freely among them.

sentences.zh: 因聽自首，先有奸通婦女及尼、女冠等，並即配之。

translations.literal: He also allowed self-reporting: those who had previously had illicit relations with women, nuns, or female Daoist adepts were immediately matched with them.
translations.idiomatic: He also allowed men to confess prior affairs with women, nuns, or female Daoist adepts and had them married on the spot.

sentences.zh: 由是驍果等悅，鹹相謂曰：「裴公之惠也。」

translations.literal: From this the Valiant Corps were pleased and all said to one another: "This is Lord Pei's kindness."
translations.idiomatic: The Valiant Corps were overjoyed and said among themselves, "This is Lord Pei's bounty."

sentences.zh: 宇文化及之亂，矩晨起將朝，至坊門，遇逆黨數人，控矩馬詣孟景所。

translations.literal: During Yuwen Huaji's rebellion, Ju rose early intending to attend court; at the ward gate he met several rebels who seized his horse's reins and took him to Meng Jing's place.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuwen Huaji rebelled, Ju rose early to attend court; at the ward gate rebels seized his bridle and dragged him to Meng Jing's house.

sentences.zh: 賊皆曰：「不關裴黃門。

translations.literal: The rebels all said: "This does not concern Vice Director Pei.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels said, "This has nothing to do with Vice Director Pei."

sentences.zh: 」既而化及從百餘騎至，矩迎拜，化及慰諭之。

translations.literal: " Before long Huaji arrived with more than a hundred riders; Ju went out to bow, and Huaji comforted and reassured him.
translations.idiomatic: " Soon Huaji arrived with more than a hundred riders; Ju bowed to him, and Huaji spoke words of reassurance.

sentences.zh: 令矩參定儀注，推秦王子浩為帝，以矩為侍內，隨化及至河北。

translations.literal: He had Ju help fix the ceremonial regulations, set up Prince Hao of Qin as emperor, appointed Ju as Palace Attendant, and Ju followed Huaji to Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: He had Ju help draft the court ritual, installed Prince Hao of Qin as emperor, made Ju Palace Attendant, and Ju followed Huaji north to Hebei.

sentences.zh: 及僭帝位，以矩為尚書右僕射，加光祿大夫，封蔡國公，為河北道安撫大使。

translations.literal: When Huaji usurped the throne, he made Ju Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, added the title Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, enfeoffed him as Duke of Cai, and made him Pacification Commissioner of the Hebei Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: When Huaji seized the throne, he made Ju Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, enfeoffed him as Duke of Cai, and appointed him Pacification Commissioner of the Hebei Circuit.

sentences.zh: 及宇文氏敗，為竇建德所獲，以矩隋代舊臣，遇之甚厚。

translations.literal: When the Yuwen clan fell, Ju was captured by Dou Jiande; because Ju was an old minister of the Sui, Dou treated him with great favor.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yuwen house fell, Dou Jiande captured Ju; as a veteran minister of the Sui, Ju was treated with great respect.

sentences.zh: 複以為吏部尚書，尋轉尚書右僕射，專掌選事。

translations.literal: Dou again made him Director of the Ministry of Personnel; soon after he was transferred to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, exclusively managing appointment affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Dou made him Director of the Ministry of Personnel, then soon transferred him to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, putting him in sole charge of appointments.

sentences.zh: 建德起自群盜，未有節文，矩為制定朝儀。

translations.literal: Jiande had risen from banditry and had no court ritual; Ju for him established court ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande had risen from the bandit ranks and had no court protocol; Ju drew up the court ritual for him.

sentences.zh: 旬月之間，憲章頗備，擬于王者。

translations.literal: Within a month the statutes and regulations were largely complete, approximating those of a king.
translations.idiomatic: Within a month the laws and rites were largely in place, nearly matching those of a true king.

sentences.zh: 建德大悅，每諮訪焉。

translations.literal: Jiande was greatly pleased and frequently consulted him.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande was delighted and consulted him constantly.

sentences.zh: 及建德渡河討孟海公，矩與曹旦等於洺州留守。

translations.literal: When Jiande crossed the river to campaign against Meng Haigong, Ju and Cao Dan remained to garrison at Ming Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiande crossed the river to attack Meng Haigong, Ju and Cao Dan stayed behind to hold Ming Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 建德敗于武牢。

translations.literal: Jiande was defeated at Wulao.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande was defeated at Wulao.

sentences.zh: 群帥未知所屬，曹旦長史李公淹、大唐使人魏徵等說旦及齊善行令歸順。

translations.literal: The commanders did not know whom to follow; Cao Dan's Chief Administrator Li Gongyan, Tang envoy Wei Zheng, and others persuaded Dan and Qi Shanxing to submit.
translations.idiomatic: The commanders did not know where their loyalty lay; Cao Dan's chief administrator Li Gongyan, the Tang envoy Wei Zheng, and others persuaded Dan and Qi Shanxing to surrender.

sentences.zh: 旦等從之，乃令矩與徵、公淹領旦及八璽，舉山東之地歸於大唐。

translations.literal: Dan and the rest agreed; they then had Ju, Wei, and Gongyan lead Dan and the eight seals, surrendering all the land east of the mountains to Great Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Dan agreed; Ju, Wei, and Gongyan then led Dan and the eight seals in surrendering all the lands east of the mountains to Great Tang.

sentences.zh: 授左庶子，轉詹事、民部尚書。

translations.literal: He was appointed Left Assistant to the Heir Apparent, then transferred to Grand Mentor and Director of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Left Assistant to the Heir Apparent, then promoted to Grand Mentor and Director of the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：世基初以雅淡著名，兼以文華見重，亡國羈旅，特蒙任遇。

translations.literal: The historian says: Yu Shiji was at first famous for refined simplicity and also valued for literary brilliance; a captive exile of a fallen state, he was specially favored with appointment.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Yu Shiji was first known for quiet refinement and literary grace; an exile of a ruined kingdom, he was nonetheless singled out for high office.

sentences.zh: 參機衡之職，預帷幄之謀，國危未嘗思安，君昏不能納諫。

translations.literal: He held posts at the pivots of power and took part in counsels within the tent—yet when the state was in peril he never thought to secure it, and when the ruler was benighted he could not persuade him to reform.
translations.idiomatic: He held the levers of power and sat in on secret counsel—yet when the state was dying he never sought to save it, and when the ruler was lost he could not move him with honest advice.

sentences.zh: 方更鬻官賣獄，黷貨無厭，顛隕厥身，亦其所也。

translations.literal: Instead he further sold offices and judgments, corrupt gain without end—to fall and perish was only what he deserved.
translations.idiomatic: Instead he sold offices and verdicts, grasping for profit without end; that he fell and perished was only fitting.

sentences.zh: 裴蘊素懷奸險，巧於附會，作威作福，唯利是視，滅亡之禍，其可免乎？

translations.literal: Pei Yun had long harbored treachery and cunning, was skilled at currying favor, wielded power for himself, and saw only profit—could he have escaped the calamity of destruction?
translations.idiomatic: Pei Yun had always been treacherous and cunning, adept at ingratiation, drunk on power, and greedy for gain—how could he have escaped ruin?

sentences.zh: 裴矩學涉經史，頗有幹局，至於恪勤匪懈，夙夜在公，求諸古人，殆未之有。

translations.literal: Pei Ju's learning ranged through the classics and histories and he possessed considerable capacity for affairs; as for unwearying diligence, working day and night in the state's service—sought among the ancients, perhaps none had been like him.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Ju was versed in the classics and histories and had real talent for statecraft; in tireless devotion to duty, working from dawn till night on the state's business, the ancients themselves could scarcely match him.

sentences.zh: 與聞政事，多曆歲年，雖處危亂之中，未虧廉謹之節，美矣。

translations.literal: He shared in government over many years; though he lived amid crisis and chaos, he did not lose his integrity and restraint—admirable indeed.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in government for many years; even amid crisis and chaos he never lost his integrity—a thing to admire.

sentences.zh: 然承望風旨，與時消息，使高昌入朝，伊吾獻地，聚糧且末，師出玉門，關右騷然，頗亦矩之由也。

translations.literal: Yet in deferring to the prevailing intent and shifting with the times, he helped bring Gaochang to court, Yiwu to surrender its land, grain to be stockpiled at Qiemo, armies to march from Yumen—the whole Longyou region in turmoil—and this too was largely due to Ju.
translations.idiomatic: Yet by reading the emperor's wishes and bending with the moment, he helped bring Gaochang to court, Yiwu to yield its territory, grain to pile up at Qiemo, and armies to pour through Yumen until Longyou was in uproar—and much of that, too, was Ju's doing.
